definition_zh: 怀疑的；不轻信的；对某事持保留态度的；怀疑论的；显出怀疑的
definition_en: inclined to doubt a claim until evidence supports it, or showing that doubt openly
core_image: 一张递过来的宣传单摆在桌上，一只手按住它，另一只手先去翻背面密密麻麻的小字
scene: 听证会开始前，一位委员把厚厚的报告推到一边，要求先看原始数据再表态。The committee remained skeptical of the summary until the raw records were released.
sceneCN: 这里指对某一说法持保留态度（第 1 个义项：不轻易相信的）；句意为委员会对那份摘要一直存疑，直到原始记录公布才松口。图中可辨识物件：厚报告、被推到一边的摘要、原始数据表、听证席。

pos.zh: 怀疑的；不轻信的；怀疑论的
（表情、语气）显出怀疑的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示主义、态度的名词尾构成，义为「怀疑态度；怀疑论」
由同一希腊词干构成，义为「持怀疑态度的人；怀疑论者」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「怀疑地」
英式拼写变体，义同「怀疑的」
英式拼写变体，义同「怀疑态度」

senses.title: Not easily convinced
senses.definition: refusing to accept a claim before evidence appears
senses.definitionCN: 在证据出现之前拒绝接受某个说法
senses.example: Investors were skeptical of the forecast until the third quarter numbers came out.
senses.exampleCN: 在第三季度数据公布之前，投资者对那份预测一直持怀疑态度。
senses.why: The Greek word behind it meant fond of looking closely, and looking closely is exactly what this sense asks for.
senses.whyCN: 它背后的希腊词意为「爱细看」，而这一义项要求的正是先细看再表态。

senses.title: Doubting one particular claim
senses.definition: doubting that a specific statement is true
senses.definitionCN: 怀疑某个具体陈述为真
senses.example: She was skeptical of his explanation that the delay was caused by weather.
senses.exampleCN: 他解释说延误是天气造成的，她对此表示怀疑。
senses.why: Here the doubt has an object: one named statement is held back from belief.
senses.whyCN: 这里的怀疑有明确对象：某个被点名的说法被暂时挡在信任之外。

senses.title: The habit of testing instead of accepting
senses.titleCN: 以检验代替接受的习惯
senses.definition: the working habit in research of testing claims rather than trusting them
senses.definitionCN: 研究中以检验主张代替直接相信的工作习惯
senses.example: A skeptical reviewer asked for the raw measurements behind the graph.
senses.exampleCN: 一位持怀疑态度的审稿人要求提供图表背后的原始测量数据。
senses.why: This sense names a method rather than a mood: doubt becomes a routine step in the work.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项指的不是情绪而是方法：怀疑成了工作流程里的固定一步。

senses.title: A doubtful expression
senses.definition: a look or tone that openly shows disbelief
senses.definitionCN: 公开显出不相信的神情或语气
senses.example: He raised one eyebrow and gave the salesman a skeptical look.
senses.exampleCN: 他挑起一边眉毛，用怀疑的神色看了推销员一眼。
senses.why: The feeling moves to the face, and the word can then describe the face itself.
senses.whyCN: 这种感受移到脸上，于是这个词也能直接描述那张脸。

senses.title: Doubtful about an outcome
senses.definition: doubting that something will actually happen or succeed
senses.definitionCN: 怀疑某事是否真会发生或成功
senses.example: Analysts are skeptical about a recovery before the end of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 分析人士对年底前出现复苏持怀疑态度。
senses.why: The object here is a future event, so the doubt is about likelihood rather than truth.
senses.whyCN: 这里怀疑的对象是未来的事件，所以怀疑的是可能性而不是真假。

senses.title: Unwilling to trust rank
senses.definition: unwilling to accept a person's word simply because of their position
senses.definitionCN: 不愿仅因某人的地位就接受其说法
senses.example: The young engineers were skeptical of the senior consultant's rule of thumb.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻工程师对那位资深顾问的经验法则并不买账。
senses.why: Doubt aimed at authority is a political as well as a mental act, and the word carries that edge.
senses.whyCN: 把怀疑对准权威，既是心理动作也是社会动作，这个词带着这股锋芒。

senses.title: The philosophical position
senses.definition: belonging to the philosophical view that certainty cannot be reached
senses.definitionCN: 属于「人无法获得确定知识」这一哲学立场
senses.example: The seminar compared skeptical and dogmatic answers to the same question.
senses.exampleCN: 研讨课就同一个问题比较了怀疑论与独断论的两种回答。
senses.why: Ancient skepticism suspended judgment on purpose; this sense keeps that technical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 古代怀疑论是刻意悬置判断，这一义项保留的就是那个术语含义。

senses.title: Hard to move once convinced otherwise
senses.definition: needing strong evidence before giving up an existing view
senses.definitionCN: 要有强证据才肯放弃原有看法
senses.example: He stayed skeptical of the new method long after his colleagues had switched.
senses.exampleCN: 同事早就换了方法，他仍对新方法持怀疑态度，久久不肯改口。
senses.why: Doubt can harden into a position, and then the word describes a person who will not shift easily.
senses.whyCN: 怀疑也会硬化成立场，这时词就形容一个不容易松动的人。

senses.title: Trained professional doubt
senses.definition: a disciplined habit of checking claims that comes with a profession
senses.definitionCN: 随职业训练而来的、核查主张的审慎习惯
senses.example: Auditors are professionally skeptical, so a friendly email proves nothing to them.
senses.exampleCN: 审计师出于职业习惯而存疑，所以一封热情洋溢的邮件对他们毫无说服力。
senses.why: In fields where mistakes are costly, doubt is taught as a skill rather than felt as an emotion.
senses.whyCN: 在错误代价高昂的领域，怀疑是被训练出来的技能，而不是被感受到的情绪。

intro.en: Skeptical goes back to Greek skeptikos, fond of examining, from skeptesthai, to look at or consider. The name belonged to the ancient school that suspended judgment, passed through Latin and French, and entered English as a word for both a temperament and a method. The choice between the k and c spellings is a modern habit rather than an old distinction.
intro.cn: 这个词可追到希腊语「爱考察的」，出自动词「细看、考虑」。古代把判断悬置起来的学派以此得名，词经拉丁语与法语进入英语，既指一种性情也指一种方法。现代英语里美式与英式的拼写各走一路，这是后来的习惯，并非古已有之的分野。

items.en: Skepsis meant a careful looking at something, the act of a person who examines before speaking.
items.cn: 本义是对某物的一番细看，即先看过再开口的人所做的动作。

items.en: The adjective described someone fond of examining, and it named the philosophical school that refused to settle every question.
items.cn: 这个形容词形容爱考察的人，并成为那个拒绝为一切问题下结论的学派之名。

items.en: Latin took the Greek adjective as a label for the school, keeping the idea of deliberate suspension of judgment.
items.cn: 拉丁语把这个希腊形容词借用为学派标签，保留了「有意悬置判断」的意思。

items.en: French carried the word into early modern debate, where it described both thinkers and a general temper.
items.cn: 法语把这个词带入近代早期的论争，既指思想家，也指一种普遍性情。

items.en: English adopted it as skeptical, first for the ancient school and soon for ordinary unwillingness to believe.
items.cn: 英语以这个形式吸收它，最初指古代学派，很快也指日常里的不肯轻信。

items.en: American usage settled on k while British usage kept c; the date at which the two spellings parted is uncertain.
items.cn: 美式用法自行定了一种拼法，英式用法保留了另一种；两种拼写分开的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek root or looks close; the second group names other ways of withholding belief.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊词根或形近；第二组指其他「不肯相信」的说法。

entries.definition: The British spelling of the same adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词的英式拼写。

entries.definition: The attitude or doctrine of doubting claims.
entries.definitionCN: 怀疑主张的态度或学说。

entries.definition: A person who doubts claims as a matter of habit.
entries.definitionCN: 习惯性怀疑各种说法的人。

entries.definition: Infected or causing infection; it comes from the Greek word for decay, not from looking.
entries.definitionCN: 指感染的或引起感染的；出自希腊语「腐坏」，与「细看」无关。

entries.definition: A striking public sight; its root means to look at as a spectacle, a different verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指引人注目的公开景象；其词根是「观看」，属另一动词。

entries.definition: Unsure whether something is true, often with a hint of worry.
entries.definitionCN: 指不确定某事是否为真，常带一丝担忧。

entries.definition: Causing or feeling doubt, often about honesty.
entries.definitionCN: 指令人起疑或自己存疑，常涉及诚信。

entries.definition: Suspecting that something is wrong or hidden.
entries.definitionCN: 指怀疑有错或有隐情。

entries.definition: Unable or unwilling to believe what one hears, often with surprise.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法或不愿相信所听之事，常带惊讶。

entries.definition: Still not persuaded after hearing the case.
entries.definitionCN: 指听完理由后仍未被说服。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the held-down leaflet, the raised eyebrow, the reviewer's raw data and the professional audit.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用按住传单的画面、挑起的眉毛、审稿人要原始数据与职业审计四个场景。

normal.en: A skeptical reader turns the page over before believing the headline.
normal.cn: 怀疑的读者会先把纸翻到背面，再决定信不信标题。

normal.en: One raised eyebrow is the cheapest form of cross-examination.
normal.cn: 挑一下眉毛，是最省力的交叉询问。

normal.en: Skeptical of a claim, not of the person, is the useful version.
normal.cn: 怀疑某个说法而不是某个人，才是有用的版本。

normal.en: A skeptical reviewer asks for the numbers behind the graph.
normal.cn: 持怀疑态度的审稿人，会要图表背后的数字。

normal.en: Professionally skeptical auditors treat a warm email as noise.
normal.cn: 职业性存疑的审计师，把热情邮件当作噪音。

abstract.en: Doubt is a door held ajar: it lets evidence in without letting belief run out.
abstract.cn: 怀疑是一扇虚掩的门：让证据进得来，又不让信念跑光。

abstract.en: Every field that fears error builds a small ritual of skepticism into its day.
abstract.cn: 每个害怕出错的领域，都会在日常里安放一套小小的怀疑仪式。

abstract.en: The same word covers a mood and a method, because a mood repeated becomes a method.
abstract.cn: 同一个词既指情绪又指方法，因为情绪重复久了就成了方法。

examples.en: Many scientists remain skeptical of results that no other lab has repeated.
examples.cn: 许多科学家对没有其他实验室复现的结果仍持怀疑态度。

examples.en: She gave the offer a skeptical glance and asked who would pay for the move.
examples.cn: 她怀疑地看了一眼那份报价，问搬迁费由谁出。

examples.en: A skeptical attitude is a requirement of the job, not a personality flaw.
examples.cn: 怀疑的态度是这份工作的要求，而不是性格缺陷。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯凯普提扣」：事事都要先「细看」一遍的人，别人说得再顺耳也要「扣」一下再信

root: 源于希腊语中表示「细看、考察」的动词，先指爱考察的人，再指把判断悬置起来的古代学派；词经拉丁语与法语进入英语。现代英语用不同字母拼写，是后来的习惯分化，分界年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses move from a general temper to a trained method: unwillingness to believe, doubt aimed at one claim, the research habit, the doubtful face, doubt about an outcome, distrust of rank, the philosophical school, a hardened position, and professional checking.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从一般性情走到训练有素的方法：不肯轻信、针对某个说法的怀疑、研究习惯、怀疑的神情、对结果的怀疑、不信权威、哲学学派、已经硬化的立场，以及职业性的核查。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand pins the leaflet to the table and the other hand turns it over to read the small print before nodding.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只手把传单按在桌上，另一只手先翻到背面读小字，然后才点头。

branches.en: THE HELD-BACK YES: belief is kept back until the evidence arrives.
branches.cn: 按住的「好」：证据到来之前，信任先不给出。

branches.en: THE TRAINED CHECK: the same doubt, repeated as a professional routine.
branches.cn: 训练有素的核查：同一种怀疑，重复成职业惯例。

branches.en: THE FACE AND THE FORECAST: doubt worn openly, whether about a claim or an outcome.
branches.cn: 神情与预测：无论针对说法还是结果，怀疑都写在明处。

branches.en: THE HARD POSITION: refusal to yield to rank, and refusal to yield at all.
branches.cn: 硬化的立场：不向地位让步，也不肯再让步。

branches.en: THE ANCIENT SCHOOL: judgment suspended on principle.
branches.cn: 古代学派：出于原则而悬置判断。

intro.en: Skeptical is a Greek examining word wearing an English adjective ending; its family covers the person, the attitude and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语「考察」之词加上英语形容词尾，词族覆盖「人」「态度」与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin passed the Greek label for the doubting school into French, and English took it in both spellings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语把怀疑学派的希腊标签传给法语，英语则把两种拼写都吸收了进来。

items.example: The act that gives the whole family its name.
items.exampleCN: 整个词族由这个动作得名。

items.example: The oldest member of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族里最古老的一员。

items.example: It named both a temper and a school.
items.exampleCN: 它既指一种性情，也指一个学派。

items.example: Latin fixed it as a philosophical label.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语把它固定为哲学标签。

items.example: It turns the label into an everyday adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个标签变成日常形容词。

items.example: It produces the name of the attitude.
items.exampleCN: 它构成这种态度的名称。

items.meaning: a person or thing of that kind
items.example: It produces the name of the doubting person.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「持怀疑者」的名称。

items.example: It produces the adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它构成副词。

由同一希腊词干构成，义为「持怀疑态度的人」

definition_zh: 按次序的；依次的；逐步依赖前一步的；顺序存取的；时序的；连续编号的
definition_en: arranged or happening in a fixed order, with each step coming after and depending on the one before
core_image: 装配台上一排螺栓从左到右排开，前一颗拧到位，手才移到下一颗
scene: 装配台上，工人按说明书一步接一步拧紧螺栓，前一颗没到位就不动下一颗。The assembly steps are sequential, so no bolt is tightened before the one beside it.
sceneCN: 这里指按固定次序、后一步依赖前一步（第 1 个义项：按固定次序排列的）；句意为装配步骤是依次进行的，旁边那颗没拧好之前不会去拧这一颗。图中可辨识物件：成排螺栓、装配说明书、拧紧扳手、到位标记。

pos.zh: 按次序的；依次的；逐步的
（计算机）顺序存取的；（电子）时序的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「依次地；按顺序地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「顺序性」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「顺序；一连串」
由「顺序」一词加动名词尾构成，义为「排序；测序」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「接着发生的」，较少用

senses.title: Arranged in a fixed order
senses.definition: placed or happening in an order where position matters
senses.definitionCN: 按位置有意义的固定次序放置或发生
senses.example: The manual lists five sequential steps, and skipping one breaks the seal.
senses.exampleCN: 说明书列出五个依次进行的步骤，跳过任何一步都会弄坏密封。
senses.why: The Latin stem simply means to follow, so anything that follows in line is called by this word.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的拉丁词干本义就是「跟随」，凡是在队列里跟着来的都可用它形容。

senses.title: Each step depends on the last
senses.definition: built so that a later step cannot start before the earlier one finishes
senses.definitionCN: 构造上后一步必须等前一步完成才能开始
senses.example: The process is sequential, which is why a delay at the first stage stops everything.
senses.exampleCN: 这个流程环环相扣，所以第一环节一拖，全线都停。
senses.why: Following in time hardens into depending in time: order becomes a condition, not a preference.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的跟随硬化成条件上的依赖：次序从偏好变成了前提。

senses.title: Sequential access in computing
senses.definition: reading stored data in the order it was written rather than jumping to any point
senses.definitionCN: 按写入顺序读取存储数据，而不是直接跳到任意位置
senses.example: A tape drive is a sequential access device, so finding the last file takes the longest.
senses.exampleCN: 磁带机是顺序存取设备，所以找最后一个文件最费时间。
senses.why: Computing borrowed the word because the machine must walk through every earlier item to reach the next one.
senses.whyCN: 计算机借用了这个词，因为机器必须走过前面每一项才能到达下一项。

senses.title: Sequential logic in electronics
senses.definition: circuits whose output depends on earlier inputs as well as the present one
senses.definitionCN: 输出不仅取决于当前输入、还取决于先前输入的电路
senses.example: A traffic light controller is built from sequential logic, since its next state depends on the last one.
senses.exampleCN: 交通灯控制器由时序逻辑构成，因为它下一个状态取决于上一个状态。
senses.why: Here the earlier state is remembered inside the circuit, so sequence is stored rather than merely observed.
senses.whyCN: 这里先前状态被电路记住，于是「先后」是被存下来的，而不只是被观察到的。

senses.title: Sequential decision making
senses.definition: choosing step by step, each choice made after seeing the result of the previous one
senses.definitionCN: 一步一步地做选择，每一步都在看到前一步结果之后才定
senses.example: The company used sequential decision making, approving each site only after the previous one opened.
senses.exampleCN: 公司采用序贯决策，前一个门店开业后才批下一个。
senses.why: The sense treats a string of choices as one procedure, which is the point of the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把一串选择当成一个程序来看，这正是这个形容词的着力处。

senses.title: Issued one after another
senses.definition: published or released in separate parts rather than all at once
senses.definitionCN: 分几次发布而不是一次性全部放出
senses.example: The journal published the findings in sequential parts over three months.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊用三个月分几次陆续发表这些发现。
senses.why: Release can be ordered in time too, and then the word describes the schedule rather than the content.
senses.whyCN: 发布也能按时间排序，这时词描述的是日程而不是内容。

senses.title: Sequential bilingualism
senses.definition: learning a second language after the first is already established
senses.definitionCN: 在第一种语言已经稳固之后才学第二种语言
senses.example: Sequential bilingualism describes a child who adds English after mastering another home language.
senses.exampleCN: 「先后习得」指孩子先掌握家中另一种语言，之后才加上英语。
senses.why: In language study the order of acquisition is the whole distinction, so the same word does precise work.
senses.whyCN: 在语言研究里，习得的先后就是全部区别，于是同一个词承担了精确的区分。

senses.title: Numbered without gaps
senses.definition: carrying numbers that run on without a break
senses.definitionCN: 号码一个接一个、中间不断开
senses.example: Each sample received a sequential number so the lab could prove none was lost.
senses.exampleCN: 每份样本都得到一个连续编号，实验室据此证明没有丢失任何一份。
senses.why: Numbering is the plainest visible form of order, and the word marks it as unbroken.
senses.whyCN: 编号是最直观可见的次序形式，这个词标出它是不断开的。

intro.en: Sequential comes from Latin sequi, to follow, through sequentia, a following or a sequence. English built the adjective on that stem, and the same root also gives sequence, subsequent and consequence, each taking a different prefix or ending to say what kind of following is meant.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语「跟随」，经「跟随、连续」这一名词进入英语。形容词是在该词干上构成的；同一词根还给出「顺序」「随后的」「后果」等词，各自用不同的前缀或词尾说明是哪种跟随。

items.en: Sequi meant to follow, and it stands behind a whole family of words about coming after something.
items.cn: 这个词意为「跟随」，一整族表示「在……之后」的词都由它而来。

items.en: The noun named a following, hence a series of things one after another.
items.cn: 该名词表示「跟随」，因此也指一件接一件的一串事物。

items.en: Church music used the same word for verses appended after the alleluia, an early example of following in order.
items.cn: 教会音乐用同一个词指附加在欢呼词之后的诗节，是「按序接在后面」的早期例子。

items.en: French passed the noun to English, where it named an order of events or of items in a series.
items.cn: 法语把这个名词传给英语，用来指事件或一系列项目的次序。

items.en: English added the adjective ending to the Latin stem in the seventeenth century.
items.cn: 英语在十七世纪给这个拉丁词干加上形容词词尾。

items.en: Computing and electronics took the word for data read in order and for circuits that remember earlier states; the first recorded year of each technical use is uncertain.
items.cn: 计算机与电子学分别用它指按顺序读出的数据与记住先前状态的电路；这两种技术用法各自首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin verb for following; the second group names other ways of coming one after another, and the note separates sequential from subsequent.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「跟随」动词；第二组指其他「一个接一个」的说法，并借以分清「依次」与「随后」。

entries.definition: An order of items or events; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指项目或事件的次序，是形容词背后的名词。

entries.definition: Coming after something else in time; it adds a prefix meaning under or after, so it points to one later item rather than to an internal order.
entries.definitionCN: 指在时间上紧随某事之后；它加了表示「在下、在后」的前缀，指向某一个较晚的项目而不是内部次序。

entries.definition: A result that follows from an action, with a prefix meaning together with.
entries.definitionCN: 指由某一行动引出的结果，前缀意为「连同」。

entries.definition: Following without a break; it comes from another verb meaning to follow closely, not from the same noun.
entries.definitionCN: 指连续不断的；出于另一表示「紧跟」的动词，并非同一名词。

entries.definition: Following on; the rare adjective form without the extra ending.
entries.definitionCN: 指接着发生的；不带附加词尾的少用形容词形式。

entries.definition: Following one after another, often with the sense of a series of similar items.
entries.definitionCN: 指一个接一个，常指同类项目构成的系列。

entries.definition: Arranged in a series, one at a time, as with numbers or ports.
entries.definitionCN: 指排成系列的、逐个进行的，如编号或接口。

entries.definition: Arranged according to a rule or plan.
entries.definitionCN: 指按某种规则或计划排好。

entries.definition: Done in stages, with each stage explained or completed before the next.
entries.definitionCN: 指分阶段进行，每阶段完成后再进下一阶段。

entries.definition: Proceeding in a straight line of steps without branching.
entries.definitionCN: 指沿着一条不回头的步骤线推进。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the bolt row, the manual's steps, the tape drive and the unbroken numbering.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用成排螺栓、说明书的步骤、磁带机与不间断的编号。

normal.en: A sequential process is a queue, not a crowd: nobody moves out of turn.
normal.cn: 依次的流程是队列而不是人群：没人能插队。

normal.en: If the first step stalls, every later step waits, because order is also dependence.
normal.cn: 第一步卡住，后面的每一步都等着，因为次序同时是依赖。

normal.en: A tape must walk past every earlier file to reach yours.
normal.cn: 磁带必须走过前面每个文件，才够到你那一个。

normal.en: Sequential numbering leaves no gap, so a missing number is proof of a lost item.
normal.cn: 连续编号不留空档，跳号就证明丢了东西。

normal.en: Sequential is about the order inside a line; subsequent is about one thing landing after another.
normal.cn: 「依次」说的是队列内部的次序，「随后」说的是某物落在另一物之后。

abstract.en: Order is a promise that the next thing will not arrive before the last one has finished.
abstract.cn: 次序是一个承诺：下一件事不会在上件事结束前到来。

abstract.en: A society runs on sequential rules it never notices, until two things try to happen at once.
abstract.cn: 社会靠无数不被注意的先后规则运转，直到两件事试图同时发生。

abstract.en: Following is neutral; the prefix decides whether you follow behind, follow with, or follow on.
abstract.cn: 「跟随」本身是中性的，前缀决定你是跟在后面、跟着一起，还是接着往下。

examples.en: Please follow the sequential steps in the order given, not in the order you prefer.
examples.cn: 请按给出的次序完成这些步骤，而不是按你喜欢的次序。

examples.en: The interview moved through sequential stages, and each stage was scored before the next began.
examples.cn: 面试按阶段依次进行，每一阶段先打分，再进入下一阶段。

examples.en: Files on the old tape are stored in sequential order, so a search can take several minutes.
examples.cn: 旧磁带上的文件按顺序存放，因此检索可能要花好几分钟。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「西宽小」：事情得按「先来后到」排成一列，一步「宽」出格，后面的全乱

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「跟随」的动词，其名词义为「跟随、连续」，形容词即在此词干上构成。同一词根还给出表示「顺序」「随后」「后果」的词；其中表示「随后」的那个加了「在后」的前缀，只指某一个较晚的项目，而这个词指队列内部的先后。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses run from plain order to technical order: fixed arrangement, step-by-step dependence, sequential access, sequential logic, sequential decisions, staged release, sequential bilingualism, and unbroken numbering.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从普通次序走到技术次序：固定排列、环环相扣、顺序存取、时序逻辑、序贯决策、分期发布、先后习得语言，以及连续编号。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the bolts sit in a row, and the hand may only move after the previous bolt is tight.
core.cn: 核心意象：螺栓排成一列，前一颗拧紧之后，手才允许移动。

branches.en: THE QUEUE AND ITS LOCK: position in line, then dependence on the previous step.
branches.cn: 队列与锁：先有队列中的位置，再有对前一步的依赖。

branches.en: THE MACHINE'S MEMORY: data read in stored order, and circuits that keep an earlier state.
branches.cn: 机器的记忆：按存储次序读取数据，电路记住先前状态。

branches.en: THE STAGGERED SCHEDULE: choices and releases that come out one at a time.
branches.cn: 错开的日程：选择与发布都一个一个出来。

branches.en: THE SECOND LANGUAGE AFTER THE FIRST: acquisition ordered in time.
branches.cn: 先母语后第二语言：习得按时间排序。

branches.en: THE NUMBER WITHOUT A GAP: order made visible.
branches.cn: 不断号的数字：被看得见的次序。

intro.en: Sequential is a Latin following stem with three English endings around it; the same stem supplies the nouns and verbs of ordering.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「跟随」词干套上英语词尾；同一词干还提供表示「排序」的名词与动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies sequi and sequentia, and the prefix family shows how many kinds of following the root can name.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了「跟随」动词与名词；前缀家族则显示这个词根能命名多少种「跟随」。

items.example: The root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族的词根。

items.example: It gave English sequence.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语的「顺序」。

items.example: The stem seen in sequent and consequent.
items.exampleCN: 见于「接着的」与「随之而来的」两词。

items.example: It marks the adjective as relating to order.
items.exampleCN: 它标明该形容词与次序有关。

items.example: The everyday adverb of procedure.
items.exampleCN: 这是描述流程时最常用的副词。

items.example: It makes subsequent mean coming later.
items.exampleCN: 它使「随后的」表示较晚发生。

items.example: It makes consequence a result that comes along.
items.exampleCN: 它使「后果」成为随之而来的结果。

items.example: It closes the noun of consequence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成表示结果的「后果」名词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「依次地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「顺序性」
由同一拉丁名词构成，义为「顺序；一连串」
由「顺序」加动名词尾构成，义为「排序；测序」

definition_zh: 空间的；与位置和距离有关的；空间布局的；空间能力的；空间分布的
definition_en: relating to space, to the position and distance of things, or to the layout of an area
core_image: 总平面图摊在桌上，两栋楼之间留出的空地正被尺子一段段量过去
scene: 两名建筑师摊开总平面图，用尺子量两栋楼之间留出的那段空地。The spatial layout of the campus keeps classrooms away from the noisy road.
sceneCN: 这里指与位置、距离和布局有关（第 1 个义项：与空间有关的）；句意为校园的空间布局让教室远离嘈杂的道路。图中可辨识物件：总平面图、比例尺、两栋楼之间的空地、道路。

pos.zh: 空间的；与空间位置有关的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在空间上；按空间分布」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「空间性」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「空间；空地」
由同一拉丁词干经法语构成，义为「宽敞的」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使空间化；按空间来组织」

senses.title: Relating to space
senses.definition: concerned with space, distance and the position of objects
senses.definitionCN: 涉及空间、距离与物体位置的
senses.example: Architects study the spatial relations between rooms, not just their sizes.
senses.exampleCN: 建筑师研究房间之间的空间关系，而不只是各自的面积。
senses.why: The Latin noun for space or room gives the adjective its whole frame of reference.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「空间、空地」的名词，为这个形容词提供了整套参照框架。

senses.title: Spatial ability
senses.definition: the mental skill of picturing shapes, positions and how they would turn
senses.definitionCN: 在脑中想象形状、位置及其旋转方式的心理能力
senses.example: Pilots are tested on spatial ability before they are allowed to fly alone.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员在获准单飞之前要接受空间能力测试。
senses.why: The sense names a capacity rather than a property, though it keeps the same adjective form.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项命名的是一种能力而不是属性，但形容词形式不变。

senses.title: Spatial arrangement
senses.definition: the way objects are placed in relation to one another
senses.definitionCN: 物体彼此相对摆放的方式
senses.example: The spatial arrangement of the shelves puts the heavy items at waist height.
senses.exampleCN: 货架的空间布局把重物放在齐腰高的位置。
senses.why: Here the word describes a plan of positions, which is the most visible use of space.
senses.whyCN: 这里词描述的是一份位置方案，是「空间」最直观的用法。

senses.title: Spatial data
senses.definition: information tied to a physical location on a map or in a coordinate system
senses.definitionCN: 与地图上的物理位置或坐标系绑定的信息
senses.example: The map team combines spatial data with rainfall records to predict flooding.
senses.exampleCN: 制图团队把空间数据与降雨记录结合，用来预测洪水。
senses.why: The phrase turns location into a variable, so the adjective marks data that carries coordinates.
senses.whyCN: 这一说法把位置变成变量，形容词于是标出「自带坐标」的数据。

senses.title: Spatial memory
senses.definition: the memory of where things are and how to get back to them
senses.definitionCN: 记住物品所在位置以及如何回到那里的记忆
senses.example: Rats in the maze rely on spatial memory rather than on marks on the floor.
senses.exampleCN: 迷宫里的老鼠靠空间记忆，而不是靠地面上的标记。
senses.why: Memory can hold a map as well as a list, and this sense names that map.
senses.whyCN: 记忆能装下一张地图，也能装下列表，这一义项命名的正是地图。

senses.title: Spatial reasoning
senses.definition: solving problems by imagining movement, rotation and overlap
senses.definitionCN: 通过想象移动、旋转与叠合来解决问题
senses.example: The test measures spatial reasoning by asking which shape a folded sheet would make.
senses.exampleCN: 这项测试让人判断折叠后的纸片会是什么形状，以测量空间推理。
senses.why: Reasoning about unseen positions is a separate skill, so it earns its own sense.
senses.whyCN: 对看不见的位置进行推理是一项独立技能，因此单独成义。

senses.title: Spatial awareness
senses.definition: noticing where one's body is in relation to nearby objects
senses.definitionCN: 注意自身身体与近旁物体的相对位置
senses.example: A cyclist needs spatial awareness to judge the gap between the handlebars and a parked van.
senses.exampleCN: 骑车人需要空间意识，才能判断车把与停着的货车之间还剩多少空隙。
senses.why: Awareness adds the body to the map, so the sense moves from objects to one's own outline among them.
senses.whyCN: 「意识」把身体也放进地图，于是义项从物体移到自身在物体之间的轮廓。

senses.title: Spatial distribution
senses.definition: the way a feature is spread across an area
senses.definitionCN: 某一特征在一区域内散布的方式
senses.example: The spatial distribution of the wells shows a gap in the eastern half of the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 水井的空间分布显示出河谷东半部存在空白。
senses.why: Distribution adds a pattern in space, which is why the adjective is needed.
senses.whyCN: 「分布」加上空间中的模式，这正是需要这个形容词的原因。

intro.en: Spatial comes from Latin spatium, space or room, through the later adjective spatialis and French spatial. English adopted it in the seventeenth century for matters of extent and position, and it now pairs naturally with words like layout, reasoning and data.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 spatium「空间、空地」，经后起的形容词与法语进入英语。英语在十七世纪把它用于广延与位置之事，如今与「布局」「推理」「数据」等词自然搭配。

items.en: Spatium named an open stretch, a room, a distance, or a period of time.
items.cn: 这个词表示一段开阔地、一处空地、一段距离，也可以指一段时间。

items.en: Later Latin formed an adjective meaning belonging to space.
items.cn: 后起的拉丁语构成形容词，意为「属于空间的」。

items.en: French used the adjective in geometry and philosophy before English borrowed it.
items.cn: 法语在几何与哲学中使用该形容词，早于英语借入。

items.en: English applied it to extent, position and the arrangement of bodies in the physical world.
items.cn: 英语把它用于广延、位置以及物体在物理世界中的排列。

items.en: Geography, psychology and computing each added a compound use, such as spatial data and spatial reasoning.
items.cn: 地理学、心理学与计算机各自加上复合用法，如空间数据与空间推理。

items.en: A shorter spelling without the second vowel also appears, but the standard form keeps it; the variant's first recorded date is uncertain.
items.cn: 少一个元音的较短拼写也出现过，但标准形式保留了它；该变体首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the Latin word for space or looks close; the second group names other ways of describing position. The note also sets spatial against temporal, its usual opposite.
note.cn: 第一组共享拉丁语「空间」或形近；第二组指其他描述位置的说法。这里也把「空间的」与「时间的」这组常用对立说清。

entries.definition: The noun for room or extent; the source of the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 指空地或广延的名词，是形容词的来源。

entries.definition: Having plenty of room inside.
entries.definitionCN: 指内部宽敞、空间充足的。

entries.definition: The quality of being laid out in space.
entries.definitionCN: 指在空间中铺展的性质。

entries.definition: A rarer spelling of the same adjective, without the second vowel.
entries.definitionCN: 同一形容词较少见的拼写，少一个元音。

entries.definition: Particular or exceptional; its root means a kind or appearance, not space.
entries.definitionCN: 指特殊的、特别的；其词根意为「种类、外观」，与空间无关。

entries.definition: Relating to time rather than to space; the two words mark the two axes of measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指与时间有关而非空间；两词标出测量所用的两条轴。

entries.definition: Relating to places on the earth's surface, often with names and boundaries.
entries.definitionCN: 指与地表地点有关，常涉及名称与边界。

entries.definition: Relating to rank or placement rather than to space as a whole.
entries.definitionCN: 指与位置或位次有关，而不一定指整体空间。

entries.definition: Relating to measurements of length, width and height.
entries.definitionCN: 指与长宽高的度量有关。

entries.definition: Relating to the extent of a region, used mainly in geography.
entries.definitionCN: 指与区域面积有关，主要用于地理学。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the site plan, the folded sheet test, the shelf layout and the well map.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用总平面图、折纸测验、货架布局与水井分布图。

normal.en: Spatial questions ask where, not when.
normal.cn: 空间问题问的是「在哪里」，不是「什么时候」。

normal.en: A folded sheet turned in the mind is spatial reasoning at its smallest scale.
normal.cn: 在脑中旋转一张折纸，就是最小尺度的空间推理。

normal.en: Spatial memory is a map stored without paper.
normal.cn: 空间记忆是一张不用纸的地图。

normal.en: The layout of a room decides the path people take without thinking.
normal.cn: 房间的布局决定了人们不假思索走的那条路。

normal.en: Spatial data always carries a pair of coordinates.
normal.cn: 空间数据总带着一对坐标。

abstract.en: Space is the stage; time is the clock; the two adjectives keep the stage and the clock apart.
abstract.cn: 空间是舞台，时间是时钟，两个形容词把舞台与时钟分开。

abstract.en: A map is space made speakable, which is why spatial words so often borrow from drawing.
abstract.cn: 地图是被说得出口的空间，所以空间类词常从绘图借来。

abstract.en: Every crowded room is a spatial argument that nobody has written down.
abstract.cn: 每一间拥挤的屋子，都是一场没人写下来的空间辩论。

examples.en: The team mapped the spatial distribution of the species across the valley.
examples.cn: 团队绘制了该物种在河谷内的空间分布。

examples.en: Children who read early often show strong spatial skills.
examples.cn: 较早识字的孩子常表现出较强的空间能力。

examples.en: Any spatial change to the hall must be approved by the safety office.
examples.cn: 大厅任何空间上的改动都须经安全部门批准。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「斯佩舍」：眼睛先「舍」得退后一步，才看得清东西在「空间」里怎么摆

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「空间、空地、距离」的名词，后起形容词义为「属于空间的」，再经法语进入英语。同族有表示「空间」与「宽敞」的词。十七世纪进入英语；各领域复合用法为后来扩展。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from plain position to trained skills: space itself, spatial ability, arrangement, data, memory, reasoning, body awareness, and distribution.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从普通位置走到训练出的技能：空间本身、空间能力、布局、数据、记忆、推理、身体意识与分布。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ruler walks across the gap between two buildings on a site plan.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把尺子在总平面图上量过两栋楼之间的那段空隙。

branches.en: THE STAGE AND THE PLAN: space itself, then a deliberate arrangement inside it.
branches.cn: 舞台与方案：先是空间本身，再是空间里的有意安排。

branches.en: THE MIND'S ROTATION: ability, memory and reasoning about unseen positions.
branches.cn: 心中的旋转：对看不见的位置的能力、记忆与推理。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SURFACE: coordinates on a map and the pattern they form over an area.
branches.cn: 被测量的地表：地图上的坐标及其在区域内形成的模式。

branches.en: THE MAP KEPT IN MEMORY: where things are and how to return.
branches.cn: 记在脑里的地图：东西在哪、怎么回去。

branches.en: THE BODY IN THE ROOM: awareness of one's own outline among objects.
branches.cn: 房间里的身体：对自身轮廓与周围物体的意识。

intro.en: Spatial is a Latin space noun plus one adjective ending; the family covers room, extent and the adverb of placement.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「空间」名词加一个形容词尾；词族覆盖空地、广延与表示位置的副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin spatium supplies the noun of room and distance, and later Latin made the adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语中表示空地、距离的名词提供词干，后起拉丁语构成形容词。

items.example: The root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族的词根。

items.example: It gives the English adjective its shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语形容词的形态。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把该词标为形容词。

items.example: It produces spatially.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「在空间上」。

items.example: It produces spatiality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「空间性」。

items.example: The common noun behind the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族后面的常用名词。

items.example: It forms spacious, full of room.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「宽敞的」。

items.example: The everyday form in research writing.
items.exampleCN: 这是研究写作里的常用副词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在空间上」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「空间性」
由同一拉丁词干经法语构成，义为「宽敞的」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使空间化」

definition_zh: 时间的；时间先后上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的；（解剖）颞的
definition_en: relating to time or to the order of events, and, in another line of the same spelling, relating to temples of the head or to worldly affairs
core_image: 档案柜的抽屉按年份一层层往下排，同一件事的三份记录落在三个不同的格子里
scene: 档案室里，三份记录同一事件的文件夹按年份排成一列，谁在前谁在后一眼可见。Researchers tracked the temporal order of the three events rather than the distance between them.
sceneCN: 这里指事件在时间上的先后（第 2 个义项：时间先后次序）；句意为研究者追踪三个事件的时间先后，而不是它们之间的空间距离。图中可辨识物件：按年份排列的档案夹、三份记录、年份标签、档案柜。

pos.zh: 时间的；时间上的；世俗的；尘世短暂的
（解剖）颞的；太阳穴部位的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在时间上；按时间」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「时间性；暂时性」
由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
解剖学中由同一部位名词构成的名称，指颞肌
由表示「在上」的前缀加该解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

senses.title: Relating to time
senses.definition: concerned with time as a dimension
senses.definitionCN: 涉及时间这一维度的
senses.example: The study measures temporal change rather than differences between places.
senses.exampleCN: 该研究测量的是随时间发生的变化，而不是地方之间的差异。
senses.why: The Latin word for time gives this adjective its broadest frame, and most other senses narrow it.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语中表示「时间」的词给出最宽的框架，其余义项大多是在此之上收窄。

senses.title: Order of events in time
senses.definition: the sequence in which events happen
senses.definitionCN: 事件发生的先后顺序
senses.example: The notes record the temporal order of the symptoms, not their severity.
senses.exampleCN: 记录写的是症状出现的时间先后，而不是轻重。
senses.why: Order needs an axis, and time supplies one; this sense is the everyday core.
senses.whyCN: 次序需要一个轴，时间提供了这个轴，这是最日常的核心义。

senses.title: Time resolution
senses.definition: how finely an instrument or dataset divides time
senses.definitionCN: 仪器或数据集把时间切分的精细程度
senses.example: The camera's temporal resolution is one frame every ten milliseconds.
senses.exampleCN: 这台相机的时间分辨率是每十毫秒一帧。
senses.why: Here time is measured as a grid, so the word marks the fineness of that grid.
senses.whyCN: 这里时间被当成一张网格来量，词于是标出网格的细密程度。

senses.title: The temporal lobe of the brain
senses.definition: the lobe at the side of the head, named from the temples
senses.definitionCN: 位于头侧、因太阳穴部位得名的脑叶
senses.example: The temporal lobe handles much of what we hear and remember.
senses.exampleCN: 颞叶负责我们所听到与记住的很大一部分内容。
senses.why: This sense belongs to a different Latin word, the plural name for the temples of the head.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项属于另一个拉丁词，即「头部太阳穴」的复数形式。

senses.title: Worldly power
senses.definition: authority over worldly affairs as opposed to spiritual authority
senses.definitionCN: 对世俗事务的管辖权，与属灵权力相对
senses.example: The dispute was over temporal power, not over doctrine.
senses.exampleCN: 争论针对的是世俗权力，而不是教义。
senses.why: The church set the authority of this world against the authority of the next, and the word carried the contrast.
senses.whyCN: 教会把此世的权力与彼世的权力对立起来，这个词就承载了这组对照。

senses.title: Earthly and passing
senses.definition: belonging to this world and therefore not lasting
senses.definitionCN: 属于此世、因而不能长久的
senses.example: Monks renounced temporal goods but kept their books.
senses.exampleCN: 修士舍弃尘世的财物，却留下了书。
senses.why: The same axis of time carries a judgement: what is in time will pass.
senses.whyCN: 同一条时间轴带上了判断：凡在时间之中的都会过去。

senses.title: A clause of time
senses.definition: a subordinate clause saying when something happens
senses.definitionCN: 说明某事何时发生的从属分句
senses.example: The sentence opens with a temporal clause introduced by after.
senses.exampleCN: 这个句子以表示「之后」的连接词引导的时间从句开头。
senses.why: Grammar names by function, so any clause marking time takes the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 语法按功能命名，凡标出时间的分句都用这个形容词。

senses.title: Temporal scale
senses.definition: the length of time over which something is observed
senses.definitionCN: 观察某事所跨的时间长度
senses.example: Climate and soil form on very different temporal scales.
senses.exampleCN: 气候与土壤在以极为不同的时间尺度形成。
senses.why: Scale is the length of the ruler, and on the time axis the ruler is a span of years.
senses.whyCN: 尺度就是尺子的长度；放在时间轴上，这把尺子就是一段年份。

intro.en: Temporal is two words wearing one shape. The time sense comes from Latin tempus, time, and its adjective temporalis, which also supplied the church's word for worldly affairs. The anatomy sense comes from Latin tempora, the temples of the head, a different word. English merged them in spelling, not in origin.
intro.cn: 这个词其实是两个词穿了同一件外衣。时间义来自拉丁语 tempus「时间」及其形容词，教会又用它指世俗事务。解剖义来自拉丁语 tempora「头部太阳穴」，是另一个词。英语只是在拼写上把它们合在一起，来源并不相同。

items.en: Tempus meant time, with the stem tempor- appearing in all other cases.
items.cn: 这个词意为「时间」，其余各格都用表示「时间」的词干。

items.en: The adjective meant belonging to time, and the church used it for what belongs to this world.
items.cn: 该形容词意为「属于时间的」，教会用它指属于此世的事物。

items.en: A separate noun, plural of tempus in the sense of the temples of the head, gave the anatomical word.
items.cn: 另一个名词，即「太阳穴」义的复数，给出了解剖学上的这个词。

items.en: French kept the church contrast between the worldly and the spiritual.
items.cn: 法语保留了教会关于「世俗」与「属灵」的对照。

items.en: English took both senses, and later added the grammatical and scientific uses.
items.cn: 英语把两个义项都吸收进来，后来又加上语法与科学用法。

items.en: Measurement and neuroscience gave the word new compounds; the first dates of those compounds are uncertain.
items.cn: 测量与神经科学又给出新的复合说法；这些说法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the time root or looks close; the second group names time, worldliness and related ideas. The note also contrasts temporal with spatial, and separates the time sense from the anatomy sense.
note.cn: 第一组共享「时间」词根或形近；第二组指时间、世俗及相关概念。这里也把「时间的」与「空间的」对照说清，并分开时间义与解剖义。

entries.definition: Lasting only for a time; the same time root with an ending meaning lasting for a period.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续一段时间；同一时间词根加表示「持续一段」的词尾。

entries.definition: For a limited time only.
entries.definitionCN: 指仅在有限时间内。

entries.definition: The speed of music, from the Italian use of the time word.
entries.definitionCN: 指音乐的速度，来自意大利语对「时间」一词的使用。

entries.definition: Existing at the same time; the prefix means with.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时存在的；前缀意为「共同」。

entries.definition: To stall or act evasively in order to gain time.
entries.definitionCN: 指为争取时间而拖延或见风使舵。

entries.definition: Relating to space, the other axis of measurement.
entries.definitionCN: 指与空间有关，是测量所用的另一条轴。

entries.definition: Arranged by date, with explicit times attached.
entries.definitionCN: 指按日期排列，并明确标出时间。

entries.definition: Concerned with this world rather than with religion.
entries.definitionCN: 指关心此世而非宗教事务。

entries.definition: Concerned with material life and its affairs.
entries.definitionCN: 指关注物质生活及其事务。

entries.definition: Lasting only a short time and then gone.
entries.definitionCN: 指只持续很短时间便消失。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the dated file drawers, the framework of the church, the temple-side lobe and the frame rate of a camera.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用按年份排的档案抽屉、教会与世俗的对照、头侧的脑叶以及相机的帧率。

normal.en: Temporal questions ask when, the mirror of spatial questions asking where.
normal.cn: 时间类问题问「什么时候」，正好映照空间类问题的「在哪里」。

normal.en: A temporal clause is a subordinate sentence that answers when.
normal.cn: 时间从句就是回答「何时」的从属句。

normal.en: The temporal lobe sits beside the temples, which is exactly what its Latin name says.
normal.cn: 颞叶位于太阳穴旁，它的拉丁名称说的正是这件事。

normal.en: Temporal power is the church's word for the authority of this world.
normal.cn: 世俗权力是教会用来指此世权威的说法。

normal.en: Temporal scale decides what looks fast and what looks slow.
normal.cn: 时间尺度决定什么看起来快、什么看起来慢。

abstract.en: Time is the axis that makes order visible, and this adjective is the name of that axis.
abstract.cn: 时间是把次序变可见的那条轴，而这个形容词就是这条轴的名字。

abstract.en: Two unrelated Latin nouns ended up with the same English spelling, and only the context tells them apart.
abstract.cn: 两个互不相干的拉丁名词最后拼成了一个英语单词，只能靠上下文分开。

abstract.en: Anything inside time is already leaving, which is why the worldly sense carries a hint of loss.
abstract.cn: 凡在时间之中的都已开始离去，所以世俗义总带一丝失去的意味。

examples.en: The two records differ in temporal order but agree on content.
examples.cn: 这两份记录在时间先后上不同，内容却一致。

examples.en: Temporal power and spiritual authority were once argued in the same courtroom.
examples.cn: 世俗权力与属灵权威曾在一间法庭上被同时争辩。

examples.en: Fossils and languages change on completely different temporal scales.
examples.cn: 化石与语言以完全不同的时间尺度变化。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦泼若」：先问「时间」什么时候到，再问「尘土」什么时候散，一事一时都记在案上

root: 一支源于拉丁语中表示「时间」的名词及其形容词，教会又引申指「世俗的」；另一支源于拉丁语中表示「头部太阳穴」的复数名词，给出解剖学的「颞的」。两支同形异源，英语只在拼写上合并。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses use two roots: time, its order, its resolution and scale; the anatomy of the temples; worldly power and worldly transience; and the grammar of when.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项分属两个词根：时间本身、时间次序、时间分辨率与时间尺度；太阳穴部位的解剖；世俗权力与尘世短暂；以及表示「何时」的语法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: three folders for one event slide into year-labelled drawers, and the order is visible at a glance.
core.cn: 核心意象：同一事件的三份档案滑进标着年份的抽屉，先后一眼可见。

branches.en: THE AXIS AND ITS ORDER: time as a dimension, then events placed along it.
branches.cn: 轴与轴上的次序：先是时间这一维度，再是沿它摆放的事件。

branches.en: THE MEASURED SPAN: fine resolution at one end, long scale at the other.
branches.cn: 被丈量的跨度：一端是精细分辨率，一端是长尺度。

branches.en: THE TEMPLES' LOBE: a second Latin root hiding under the same spelling.
branches.cn: 太阳穴的脑叶：同一拼写之下藏着第二个拉丁词根。

branches.en: THE WORLD AND ITS PASSING: authority here, and the fact that it fades.
branches.cn: 此世与其消逝：这里的权力，以及它终将褪去。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE OF WHEN: grammar marking time in a sentence.
branches.cn: 「何时」从句：语法在句中标出时间。

intro.en: Temporal is a Latin time noun with an adjective ending; its family covers lasting for a time, the musical tempo, and the anatomy of the temples.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「时间」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖「暂时的」、音乐的速度，以及太阳穴的解剖。

latinIntro.en: Latin tempus and its stem tempor- supply the time line, while the plural tempora supplies the anatomy line.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「时间」及其词干提供时间这一线，而复数形式「太阳穴」提供解剖这一线。

items.example: The source of the time sense.
items.exampleCN: 这是时间义的来源。

items.example: The stem seen in temporal and temporary.
items.exampleCN: 见于「时间的」与「暂时的」两词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: A separate word behind the anatomy sense.
items.exampleCN: 解剖义背后是另一个词。

items.example: It marks both senses as adjectives.
items.exampleCN: 它把两个义项都标为形容词。

items.example: It forms temporary, lasting for a time.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「暂时的」。

items.example: It forms temporality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「时间性」。

items.example: It forms temporally.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「在时间上」。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在时间上」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「时间性」
由该形容词与表示脑叶的名词构成，义为「颞叶」
由表示「在上」的前缀加解剖义构成，义为「颞上的」

definition_zh: 可触摸的；有形的；确实可指的；实际可见的；物质的
definition_en: able to be touched or clearly perceived, and therefore real enough to count or point to
core_image: 仓库里一只木箱被搬上秤台，箱面的编号和重量当场被抄进验收单
scene: 验收员戴上手套，把一只木箱搬上秤台，重量和编号当场核对。The auditors asked for tangible assets they could count in the warehouse.
sceneCN: 这里指有实体形态、可以点数核对的资产（第 2 个义项：有形资产）；句意为审计人员要求清点仓库里能实际数出来的有形资产。图中可辨识物件：木箱、秤台、验收单、编号标签、手套。

pos.zh: 可触摸的；有形的；确实的；物质的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「可触知地；确实地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「可触知性；有形性」
由表示否定的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「无形的；难以捉摸的」
同上，作名词义为「无形资产」
由同一拉丁动词的另一名词形式构成，义为「触觉的」

senses.title: Able to be touched
senses.definition: solid and firm enough for the hand to feel
senses.definitionCN: 坚实到能被手触摸到
senses.example: The sample is tangible, so a visitor can pick it up and weigh it.
senses.exampleCN: 这份样品可以触摸，参观者能拿起来称一称。
senses.why: The Latin verb behind the word means to touch, and this sense keeps the plain physical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 词后的拉丁动词意为「触摸」，这一义项保留的就是最直白的身体含义。

senses.title: A physical asset
senses.definition: property that exists in physical form and can be counted
senses.definitionCN: 具有实体形态、可以点数的财产
senses.example: Machinery and land are tangible assets; a brand name is not.
senses.exampleCN: 机器与土地是有形资产，品牌名称则不是。
senses.why: Accounting split property into what can be seen and what cannot, and used this word for the visible half.
senses.whyCN: 会计把财产分成看得见与看不见的两半，这个词被用来指看得见的那一半。

senses.title: Evidence one can point to
senses.definition: proof clear enough to show, not merely argued
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到可以拿出来展示、而非仅凭论证的证据
senses.example: The inspector wanted tangible evidence, such as a dated photograph of the crack.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员要的是确凿证据，比如一张标明日期的裂缝照片。
senses.why: Evidence becomes tangible when it can be laid on a table, and the word marks that shift from claim to object.
senses.whyCN: 证据一旦能摊在桌上就变得「有形」，词标出的正是从主张到实物的这一转。

senses.title: Results you can see
senses.definition: outcomes that can be observed or measured rather than only promised
senses.definitionCN: 可以观察或测量、而不只是被承诺的结果
senses.example: After six months the programme showed tangible results in three districts.
senses.exampleCN: 六个月后，该项目在三个区显示出看得见的成果。
senses.why: Results become tangible when they can be pointed at in a report rather than promised in a speech.
senses.whyCN: 成果一旦能在报告里被指出、而不只是在演讲里被承诺，就变得「有形」。

senses.title: A benefit actually felt
senses.definition: an advantage people can notice in daily life
senses.definitionCN: 人们在日常生活中能察觉到的益处
senses.example: The new bus line brought a tangible benefit to commuters on rainy days.
senses.exampleCN: 新公交线给雨天通勤的人带来了实实在在的好处。
senses.why: Benefits are often abstract, so calling one tangible is a claim that it has reached the body.
senses.whyCN: 好处通常是抽象的，说它「有形」，是在声称它已经落到了身体上。

senses.title: Physical heritage
senses.definition: the buildings, objects and sites inherited from the past
senses.definitionCN: 从过去继承下来的建筑、器物与遗址
senses.example: The fund protects tangible heritage such as temples and stone bridges.
senses.exampleCN: 该基金保护庙宇、石桥这类物质遗产。
senses.why: Heritage studies separate what stands in stone from what lives in practice, and this word names the stone.
senses.whyCN: 遗产研究把立在石头上的与活在做法里的分开，这个词指前者。

senses.title: A cost that appears in the accounts
senses.definition: a cost that shows up directly in spending records
senses.definitionCN: 直接出现在支出账目上的成本
senses.example: The tangible cost of the recall was small, but the lost trust was not.
senses.exampleCN: 召回的账面成本不大，失去的信任却不然。
senses.why: Accounting names a cost tangible when it appears as a line rather than as a lost opportunity.
senses.whyCN: 会计把以一行数字出现、而非以错失机会出现的成本称为「有形成本」。

senses.title: A difference large enough to notice
senses.definition: a change big enough to be seen or felt in practice
senses.definitionCN: 在实践中大到能被看见或感受到的改变
senses.example: Two weeks of practice made a tangible difference in her pronunciation.
senses.exampleCN: 两周的练习让她的发音有了明显可感的差别。
senses.why: When a difference can be felt, the word extends from the hand to experience itself.
senses.whyCN: 当差别能被感受到，这个词就从手延伸到经验本身。

intro.en: Tangible comes from Latin tangere, to touch, through the adjective tangibilis and French tangible. English took it in the sixteenth century for what the hand can reach, and accounting, law and heritage work later extended it to anything that can be counted or pointed at.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 tangere「触摸」，经形容词 tangibilis 与法语进入英语。十六世纪进入英语时指手能触及之物，后来会计、法律与遗产研究把它扩展到一切可点数、可指出之物。

items.en: Tangere meant to touch, and it also gave words for contact and for a contagious touch.
items.cn: 这个词意为「触摸」，也给出表示接触与「传染性接触」的词。

items.en: The adjective said what could be touched, in contrast with what could only be thought.
items.cn: 该形容词指可被触摸之物，与只能被思考之物相对。

items.en: French carried the adjective into discussions of proof and property.
items.cn: 法语把该形容词带入关于证据与财产的讨论。

items.en: English first used it for physical contact and soon for evidence that could be shown.
items.cn: 英语最初用它指身体接触，很快也指可以出示的证据。

items.en: Bookkeeping set tangible assets against intangible ones, fixing the word in finance.
items.cn: 记账把有形资产与无形资产对立，使这个词在金融里固定下来。

items.en: Museums and managers later applied it to objects and to results; the first date of each use is uncertain.
items.cn: 博物馆与管理领域后来又把它用于器物与成果；这些用法各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the touch root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of solidity. Several look-alikes are traps because their roots differ.
note.cn: 第一组共享「触摸」词根或形近；第二组指其他「实在」的说法。其中几个形近词因词根不同而容易误认。

entries.definition: Unable to be touched, as with a brand or a mood.
entries.definitionCN: 指无法触摸的，如品牌或气氛。

entries.definition: In a way that can be felt or shown.
entries.definitionCN: 指以能被感受或展示的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being touchable or provable.
entries.definitionCN: 指可触摸或可证实的性质。

entries.definition: A line that touches a curve at one point.
entries.definitionCN: 指只在一个点接触曲线的直线。

entries.definition: To twist into knots; it is a Scandinavian word, unrelated to touching.
entries.definitionCN: 指缠成一团；来自斯堪的纳维亚语，与「触摸」无关。

entries.definition: Relating to the sense of touch.
entries.definitionCN: 指与触觉有关的。

entries.definition: So strong or real that it seems almost touchable.
entries.definitionCN: 指强烈或真实到几乎可触摸。

entries.definition: Specific and based on real cases rather than general claims.
entries.definitionCN: 指具体、以真实案例为依据而非泛泛而谈。

entries.definition: Able to be noticed by the senses, not necessarily by touch.
entries.definitionCN: 指能被感官察觉，不一定靠触摸。

entries.definition: Belonging to the body or to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于身体或物质的。

entries.definition: Large enough or clear enough to be measured.
entries.definitionCN: 指大到或清楚到可以测量。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the weighing platform, the warehouse count, the dated photograph and the felt benefit.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用称重台、仓库清点、带日期的照片与能感受到的好处。

normal.en: If you can put it on a scale, it is tangible.
normal.cn: 能放上秤的东西，就是有形的。

normal.en: Tangible assets can be counted in a warehouse, unlike a reputation.
normal.cn: 有形资产能在仓库里点清，名声却不能。

normal.en: A dated photograph turns a complaint into tangible evidence.
normal.cn: 一张带日期的照片，把抱怨变成确凿证据。

normal.en: A benefit becomes tangible the day someone notices it on the way to work.
normal.cn: 好处在有人上班路上察觉它的那天，才算实实在在。

normal.en: The touch root also gives tangent, the line that touches a curve.
normal.cn: 「触摸」词根还给出「切线」，即接触曲线的那条线。

abstract.en: Every abstract promise is waiting for one tangible object to stand behind it.
abstract.cn: 每个抽象承诺，都在等一件有形之物站到它身后。

abstract.en: A number becomes a thing the moment someone can point at it.
abstract.cn: 数字在有人能用手指点的瞬间，就变成了东西。

abstract.en: What cannot be touched still needs a tangible proxy to be argued about in public.
abstract.cn: 摸不着的东西，也需要一个有形替身才能在公共场合被争论。

examples.en: The plan produced tangible results within the first season.
examples.cn: 这项计划在第一个季度内就产生了看得见的成果。

examples.en: Only tangible assets were insured; the brand was covered separately.
examples.cn: 只有有形资产投了保，品牌另行投保。

examples.en: There was a tangible difference in air quality after the buses changed fuel.
examples.cn: 公交车更换燃料后，空气质量有了明显可感的差别。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦著拨」：手一伸就能「触」到、一「拨」就动的东西，才算看得见摸得着

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「触摸」的动词，其形容词义为「可触摸的」，经法语进入英语。同族有表示「切线」「触觉」「接触」与「无形」的词。十六世纪进入英语，十九世纪在会计中固定「有形资产」义；各引申义首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses move from the hand outward: touchable, physical asset, provable evidence, visible results, felt benefit, material heritage, bookable cost, and a noticeable difference.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从手向外推：可触摸、有形资产、可证实的证据、看得见的成果、可感受的好处、物质遗产、账面上的成本，以及可察觉的差别。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the crate lands on the platform and both weight and number are written down at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：木箱落在秤台上，重量与编号当场被写下。

branches.en: THE HAND AND THE PROOF: what can be touched, and what can therefore be shown.
branches.cn: 手与证据：能触摸之物，因而也是能出示之物。

branches.en: THE COUNTED PROPERTY: assets and costs that appear in the books.
branches.cn: 被点数的财产：出现在账上的资产与成本。

branches.en: THE VISIBLE OUTCOME: results and differences that someone can notice.
branches.cn: 看得见的结果：有人能注意到的成果与差别。

branches.en: THE BODY'S BENEFIT: an advantage that reaches daily life.
branches.cn: 落到身体上的好处：抵达日常生活的益处。

branches.en: THE STONE HERITAGE: buildings and objects handed down.
branches.cn: 石头上的遗产：传下来的建筑与器物。

intro.en: Tangible is a Latin touch verb with an adjective ending; the family covers proof, property and the sense of touch itself.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「触摸」动词加形容词尾；词族覆盖证据、财产与触觉本身。

latinIntro.en: Latin tangere and tangibilis supply the root and the adjective; the negative prefix in English creates the opposite word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「触摸」与其形容词提供词根与词形；英语的否定前缀则造出反义词。

items.example: The root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族的词根。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.meaning: a touch, the sense of touch
items.example: It stands behind tactile.
items.exampleCN: 它是「触觉的」背后的词。

items.example: It marks what can be touched.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「能被触摸的」。

items.example: It forms intangible.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「无形的」。

items.example: It forms tangibly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「确实地」。

items.example: It forms tangibility.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「有形性」。

items.example: A same-root word from a different verb form.
items.exampleCN: 同词根但由另一动词形式构成的词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「可触知地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「有形性」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「无形的」
由同一拉丁动词的名词形式构成，义为「触觉的」

definition_zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的；迟疑不决的
definition_en: not yet final and open to change, or done cautiously as a first test
core_image: 谈判桌上摆着一份还没定稿的备忘录，签字旁边留着一行小字：待双方董事会批准
scene: 谈判结束时，双方在一份仍可修改的备忘录上签了名，各自都留了一步退路。They reached a tentative agreement that still needed approval from both boards.
sceneCN: 这里指尚未最终确定、仍可更改（第 1 个义项：暂定的）；句意为双方达成了一份仍待两家董事会批准的初步协议。图中可辨识物件：备忘录、签名栏、一行待批准的小字、会议桌。

pos.zh: 暂定的；试探性的；初步的
（少用）试探性的尝试

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「试探性地；暂定地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「试探性；迟疑」
由同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「尝试」，属同源而非直接派生
由同一拉丁动词的另一形态经法语构成，义为「引诱；试探」，属同源而非直接派生

senses.title: Not final
senses.definition: agreed or set for now but still open to change
senses.definitionCN: 暂时确定、但仍可更改的
senses.example: The schedule is tentative and will be confirmed on Friday.
senses.exampleCN: 日程是暂定的，周五才会确认。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to try, and what is tried is not yet settled.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「尝试」，试过的东西自然还没有定下来。

senses.title: An initial agreement
senses.definition: an arrangement accepted in outline, pending formal approval
senses.definitionCN: 在要点上接受、等待正式批准的安排
senses.example: The two sides signed a tentative agreement and left the details to their lawyers.
senses.exampleCN: 双方签了一份初步协议，细节留给各自的律师。
senses.why: An agreement is tentative while the signatures still wait for approval upstairs.
senses.whyCN: 协议在签名还等着上级批准时，就是初步的。

senses.title: A testing first step
senses.definition: a cautious action taken to see how others react
senses.definitionCN: 为看看对方反应而谨慎采取的行动
senses.example: She took a tentative step into the new market before committing a full budget.
senses.exampleCN: 她先在新市场试探性地迈出一步，之后才投入全部预算。
senses.why: A step that tests the ground keeps the meaning of trying in the body.
senses.whyCN: 试探地面的一步，把「尝试」的含义落到了步子上。

senses.title: A cautious smile
senses.definition: a slight smile that asks whether it is welcome
senses.definitionCN: 轻微地笑一下，试探对方是否接受
senses.example: The new student gave a tentative smile and waited for an answer.
senses.exampleCN: 新来的学生试探性地笑了笑，等着对方回应。
senses.why: Here the uncertainty is social rather than factual, but the same caution shows.
senses.whyCN: 这里的不确定是社会性的而非事实性的，但同样的谨慎仍然可见。

senses.title: A provisional conclusion
senses.definition: a conclusion offered while evidence is still incomplete
senses.definitionCN: 在证据仍不完整时给出的结论
senses.example: Our tentative conclusion is that the effect is small, though more trials are needed.
senses.exampleCN: 我们的初步结论是效应不大，但仍需更多试验。
senses.why: A conclusion offered while data are still arriving is held provisionally by design.
senses.whyCN: 在数据仍陆续到来时给出的结论，按设计就是暂且持有的。

senses.title: A date that may move
senses.definition: a fixed date that everyone knows may be changed
senses.definitionCN: 大家都明白可能会改的已定日期
senses.example: We have a tentative date in June, subject to the permit.
senses.exampleCN: 我们暂定六月，还要看许可证。
senses.why: Setting a date provisionally is a way of planning without promising.
senses.whyCN: 把日期暂定下来，是一种「做计划但不作承诺」的办法。

senses.title: A hesitant tone
senses.definition: speaking in a way that shows one is unsure of the welcome
senses.definitionCN: 说话时显出不确定对方是否欢迎的样子
senses.example: He answered in a tentative voice, as if expecting to be corrected.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟疑地回答，好像随时准备被纠正。
senses.why: Caution moves from the plan to the voice, and the word now describes how someone speaks.
senses.whyCN: 谨慎从计划移到声音上，词于是描述一个人怎么说话。

senses.title: Exploratory in method
senses.definition: trying a small move in an unfamiliar situation before going further
senses.definitionCN: 在陌生情境里先小幅行动、再决定是否继续
senses.example: The first meetings were tentative, designed to test whether the teams could work together.
senses.exampleCN: 最初的几次会面是试探性的，用来检验两队是否能合作。
senses.why: A method is tentative when its first purpose is to find out whether it works at all.
senses.whyCN: 当一种方法的首要目的是弄清它究竟行不行，它就是试探性的。

intro.en: Tentative comes from Latin tentativus, trying or testing, from tentare, to try, a frequentative form of tendere, to stretch. English took it in the sixteenth century for statements and steps held only provisionally, and the idea of a trial has stayed at its centre.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 tentativus「尝试的、试探的」，出自动词 tentare「试」，而 tentare 是 tendere「伸展」的反复形式。十六世纪进入英语，用来指只是暂时拿出的说法与步骤，「试一试」的意思始终在核心。

items.en: Tendere meant to stretch or aim, and its repeated form described trying something again and again.
items.cn: 这个词意为「伸展、指向」，其反复形式表示一次又一次地试。

items.en: Tentare meant to try, to test, and also to attack or probe.
items.cn: 这个词意为「试、试探」，也有「进攻、探察」之意。

items.en: The adjective described what was done by way of trial rather than as a settled act.
items.cn: 该形容词形容出于尝试而非定论所做的。

items.en: French used the adjective for experiments and provisional arrangements.
items.cn: 法语用它指实验与暂定的安排。

items.en: English applied it to opinions, plans and the first movements of a cautious person.
items.cn: 英语把它用于意见、计划以及谨慎者的最初动作。

items.en: Negotiation gave the word its common phrase, tentative agreement; the phrase's first recorded year is uncertain.
items.cn: 谈判给出它最常见的搭配「初步协议」；该搭配首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the trying root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of provisional things. The note also separates tentative from tenable, which looks similar but comes from a different verb.
note.cn: 第一组共享「尝试」词根或形近；第二组指其他「暂时性」的说法。这里也把「暂定的」与形近但异源的「站得住脚的」分开。

entries.definition: In a cautious or provisional way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以试探或暂定的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being provisional or hesitant.
entries.definitionCN: 指暂定或迟疑的性质。

entries.definition: To try to do something; the same Latin verb reached English through French.
entries.definitionCN: 指尝试做某事；同一拉丁动词经法语进入英语。

entries.definition: To lure or test someone; a different form of the same Latin verb.
entries.definitionCN: 指引诱或试探某人；同一拉丁动词的另一形式。

entries.definition: Able to be defended; it comes from the verb meaning to hold, not to try.
entries.definitionCN: 指站得住脚、可辩护的；出自表示「握住」的动词，与「尝试」无关。

entries.definition: A principle held as true; from the same holding verb as tenable.
entries.definitionCN: 指被奉为真的原则；与「站得住脚」同出「握住」动词。

entries.definition: Arranged for present needs and expected to be replaced.
entries.definitionCN: 指为当前需要而设、预期会被替换的。

entries.definition: Coming before the main event as preparation.
entries.definitionCN: 指在正式活动之前、作为准备的。

entries.definition: Serving only for the time between two settled states.
entries.definitionCN: 指只在两个稳定状态之间暂时顶替的。

entries.definition: Done in order to find out rather than to settle.
entries.definitionCN: 指为了了解情况而非下定论所做的。

entries.definition: Slow to act because of uncertainty; it describes the person rather than the arrangement.
entries.definitionCN: 指因不确定而行动迟缓，描述的是人而不是安排。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the unsigned contract, the first small step, the careful smile and the June date pencilled in.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用未定稿的备忘录、试探的一小步、谨慎的微笑与用铅笔写下的六月。

normal.en: A tentative deal is written in pencil, not in ink.
normal.cn: 初步协议用铅笔写，不用墨水。

normal.en: A tentative step is a foot testing the ice before the body follows.
normal.cn: 试探性的一步，是脚先试试冰面，身体再跟上。

normal.en: A tentative smile asks a question without words.
normal.cn: 试探性的微笑，是在不用言语地问一句。

normal.en: If the date is tentative, the invitation says so and nobody is blamed.
normal.cn: 日期若为暂定，请柬上会写明，事后也没人该被责怪。

normal.en: Tentative and tenable look alike, but one means tried and the other means holdable.
normal.cn: 「暂定的」与「站得住脚的」形近，一个意为「试过」，一个意为「握得住」。

abstract.en: Provisional things are honest about their own fragility, which is why they are trusted for a while.
abstract.cn: 暂定之物坦白自己的脆弱，所以反而能被信任一阵。

abstract.en: Every firm decision began as a tentative one that someone dared to repeat.
abstract.cn: 每个确定的决定，起初都是一个有人敢重复的暂定决定。

abstract.en: To try is to leave a door open; to settle is to close it, and both have their season.
abstract.cn: 尝试是留一扇门，确定是把门关上，两者各有其时。

examples.en: The committee adopted a tentative plan and asked for cost estimates.
examples.cn: 委员会采纳了一项暂定计划，并要求提供成本估算。

examples.en: He gave a tentative nod, then asked to see the contract again.
examples.cn: 他试探性地点了点头，随后要求再看一遍合同。

examples.en: The tentative date is 12 June, subject to the venue.
examples.cn: 暂定日期是六月十二日，还要看场地。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「坦特提夫」：先「试」一下再说话，语气留半分，结论也留半分

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「伸展、指向」的动词，其反复形式义为「试、试探」，再加形容词尾，经法语进入英语。表示「尝试」「引诱」的英语词与之同源，但不是由它直接派生。十六世纪进入英语；「初步协议」这一搭配首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one caution: a provisional arrangement, an initial deal, a testing step, a cautious smile, a provisional conclusion, a movable date, a hesitant voice, and an exploratory method.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享同一种谨慎：暂定安排、初步协议、试探的一步、谨慎的微笑、初步结论、可改的日期、迟疑的语气与试探性的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signature goes on a memorandum that still carries a line asking for later approval.
core.cn: 核心意象：名字签在一份备忘录上，旁边还留着一行「待批准」。

branches.en: THE OPEN ARRANGEMENT: a plan or date that everyone knows may move.
branches.cn: 敞开的安排：人人都知道可能会变的计划或日期。

branches.en: THE FIRST VERSION: an initial deal or conclusion, subject to approval.
branches.cn: 最初版本：初步协议或结论，仍待批准。

branches.en: THE FIRST PROBE: a small action taken to read another person's reaction.
branches.cn: 探路的一步：先做一个动作，看看对方如何反应。

branches.en: THE SOCIAL HESITATION: a careful smile and a careful voice.
branches.cn: 社交上的迟疑：谨慎的微笑与谨慎的语气。

branches.en: EXPLORATORY BY METHOD: start small in an unfamiliar setting, then decide whether to continue.
branches.cn: 方法上的试探：在陌生情境里先做小步，再决定是否继续。

intro.en: Tentative is a Latin trying verb with two endings; its family covers trying, testing and the caution that goes with both.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「试」动词加词尾；词族覆盖尝试、试探以及随之而来的谨慎。

latinIntro.en: Latin tendere, tentare and tentativus trace the path from stretching to trying to provisional.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「伸展」「试」「尝试的」三词，勾出从拉伸到尝试再到暂定的路径。

items.example: The deeper root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族更深的根。

items.example: The repeated form that carries the trying sense.
items.exampleCN: 承载「尝试」义的反复形式。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the word as describing a manner.
items.exampleCN: 它标明该词描述一种方式。

items.example: It forms tentatively.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「试探性地」。

items.example: It forms tentativeness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「试探性」。

items.example: A same-root word, not a derivative of tentative.
items.exampleCN: 同源词，不是由本词派生。

items.example: Another same-root word through French.
items.exampleCN: 另一个经法语而来的同源词。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「试探性地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「试探性」
同一拉丁动词经法语构成，义为「尝试」，属同源词
同一拉丁动词另一形态经法语构成，义为「引诱」，属同源词

definition_zh: 透明的；清澈的；公开透明的；易于看穿的；显而易见的；（计算机）对用户不可见的
definition_en: allowing light through so that what lies behind can be seen, or open enough that nothing is hidden
core_image: 整面玻璃隔墙后面，会议桌、白板与争论的手势都看得清清楚楚
scene: 新会议室的隔墙换成整面玻璃，走廊上的人能看见里面开会的全过程。The ministry promised a transparent budget that any citizen could check line by line.
sceneCN: 这里指公开、可供查看（第 2 个义项：公开透明的）；句意为该部门承诺拿出一份任何公民都能逐行核对的透明预算。图中可辨识物件：玻璃隔墙、会议桌、白板、走廊上的人。

pos.zh: 透明的；公开透明的；易懂的；显而易见的
（计算机）对用户不可见的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「透明；透明度；公开性」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「透明地；显然地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「透明」，较少用
由表示「一半」的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「半透明的」

senses.title: See-through
senses.definition: letting light pass so that objects behind are visible
senses.definitionCN: 让光通过，从而使后面的物体可见
senses.example: The tank is made of transparent plastic, so the water level is visible from any side.
senses.exampleCN: 水箱用透明塑料制成，从任何一侧都能看见水位。
senses.why: The Latin parts mean to show through, and this sense keeps the plain optical meaning.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语的构件意为「透过来显现」，这一义项保留的是最直白的光学含义。

senses.title: Open and honest
senses.definition: open to inspection, with nothing important kept hidden
senses.definitionCN: 可供查看，重要信息不被隐瞒
senses.example: Voters expect a transparent account of how the money was spent.
senses.exampleCN: 选民期待一份关于钱怎么花掉的公开说明。
senses.why: The optical image becomes a moral one: what hides nothing can be seen through.
senses.whyCN: 光学的意象转成伦理的：不藏东西的东西，才经得起被看穿。

senses.title: A process anyone can follow
senses.definition: a procedure whose steps can be traced by outsiders
senses.definitionCN: 外部人也能追踪每一步的程序
senses.example: The hiring process is transparent, with criteria published before interviews begin.
senses.exampleCN: 招聘流程是透明的，标准在面试开始前就已公布。
senses.why: A process is transparent when an outsider can follow every step without asking for files.
senses.whyCN: 当外部人不必索要文件就能跟上每一步，流程就是透明的。

senses.title: Government open to view
senses.definition: public business conducted in view of the public
senses.definitionCN: 在公众视野中办理公共事务
senses.example: The city publishes its contracts online as part of a transparent government policy.
senses.exampleCN: 该市把合同公布在网上，作为政务公开政策的一部分。
senses.why: The optical word became a demand that public business be visible to the public.
senses.whyCN: 这个光学词变成一项要求：公共事务必须对公众可见。

senses.title: An excuse that fools nobody
senses.definition: an explanation so weak that its falseness is obvious
senses.definitionCN: 薄弱到虚假一看便知的解释
senses.example: Saying the dog ate the report was a transparent excuse.
senses.exampleCN: 说报告被狗吃了，是个一眼看穿的借口。
senses.why: Here see-through means the deception is visible, which is the mocking use of the word.
senses.whyCN: 这里的「看得穿」指骗局本身可见，是这个词带讽刺的用法。

senses.title: Intentions easy to read
senses.definition: motives that others can see without being told
senses.definitionCN: 别人不必被说明就能看出的动机
senses.example: His praise was transparent: he wanted the contract signed that afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 他的称赞意图明显：他想让合同当天下午就签。
senses.why: Motives that can be read off behaviour are as visible as objects behind glass.
senses.whyCN: 从行为上就能读出的动机，和玻璃后面的物体一样可见。

senses.title: Accounts that can be checked
senses.definition: financial records presented clearly enough to be verified
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到可以被核验的财务记录
senses.example: Transparent accounting let the auditors finish in two days.
senses.exampleCN: 账目清楚，让审计人员两天就完成了工作。
senses.why: Numbers presented so that any reader can redo the arithmetic are clear in the same way.
senses.whyCN: 呈现得让任何读者都能重算一遍的数字，以同样的方式「清楚」。

senses.title: Hidden from the user
senses.definition: in computing, working in the background without being visible to the user
senses.definitionCN: 计算中指在后台运行、用户看不见
senses.example: The update is transparent to the user, who only notices a faster start.
senses.exampleCN: 这次更新对用户是透明的，用户只察觉到启动变快了。
senses.why: This sense reverses the metaphor: what is transparent is not seen, because it does not get in the way.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项把比喻反过来：所谓「透明」，是因为不挡路，所以不被看见。

senses.title: Plainly true
senses.definition: so clear that no explanation is needed
senses.definitionCN: 清楚到无需解释的
senses.example: It is transparent to everyone that the two figures cannot both be right.
senses.exampleCN: 所有人都看得出来，这两个数字不可能同时成立。
senses.why: The last step of the metaphor: what needs no explanation is simply seen through.
senses.whyCN: 比喻的最后一步：无需解释的东西，就是被直接看穿的。

intro.en: Transparent is Latin trans, across, plus parere, to appear: a thing that shows itself through another. French carried the adjective into English, where it kept the optical sense and gained the moral one. The Latin verb parere that means to appear is not the same line as the look-alike verb meaning to obey.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语 trans「穿过」加 parere「显现」构成，指某物透过另一物显出自己。法语把形容词带入英语，它保留了光学义，又长出伦理义。表示「显现」的拉丁动词，与那个同形但意为「听从」的动词并非同一条线。

items.en: One Latin verb meant to come into view or appear, and it stands behind apparent and appearance.
items.cn: 有一个拉丁动词意为「出现在视野中、显现」，是「明显的」与「外观」背后的词。

items.en: The compound meant to show through, as light through water.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「透过显现」，如光穿过水。

items.en: The participle described something that lets what is behind it be seen.
items.cn: 这个分词形容能让背后的东西被看见之物。

items.en: French used it for glass and water before extending it to conduct.
items.cn: 法语先用它指玻璃与水，后扩展到行为。

items.en: English kept both the optical and the moral sense, and later added the computing one.
items.cn: 英语同时保留光学义与伦理义，后来又加上计算机用法。

items.en: Finance, government and software each gave the word a fixed phrase; the first date of each phrase is uncertain.
items.cn: 金融、政务与软件各自给出固定说法；这些说法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the showing-through root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of clarity. The note also separates transparent from translucent.
note.cn: 第一组共享「透出」词根或形近；第二组指其他「清楚」的说法，并把「透明」与「半透明」分清。

entries.definition: The quality of being see-through or open, and a film viewed on a projector.
entries.definitionCN: 指透明或公开的性质，也指投影用的胶片。

entries.definition: Seeming to be true from what is visible.
entries.definitionCN: 指从可见之处看来似乎为真。

entries.definition: The way something looks when it comes into view.
entries.definitionCN: 指某物进入视野时的样子。

entries.definition: To become known, or of plants, to lose water through leaves; its root means to breathe, not to appear.
entries.definitionCN: 指事情泄露，或植物经叶片失水；其词根意为「呼吸」而非「显现」。

entries.definition: Letting light through but not letting shapes be seen clearly; its root means to shine.
entries.definitionCN: 指透光但看不清形状；其词根意为「照耀」。

entries.definition: Easy to see through or easy to understand.
entries.definitionCN: 指易于看透或易于理解。

entries.definition: Honest and direct in speech, especially about difficulty.
entries.definitionCN: 指说话诚实直接，尤其在谈及难处时。

entries.definition: Not concealed; accessible to others.
entries.definitionCN: 指不隐瞒、对他人开放。

entries.definition: So plain that it needs no explanation.
entries.definitionCN: 指明显到不需解释。

entries.definition: Required to explain and answer for one's actions.
entries.definitionCN: 指有义务为自己的行为作出说明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the glass wall, the published budget, the transparent excuse and the invisible update.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用玻璃隔墙、公布的预算、一眼看穿的借口与看不见的更新。

normal.en: A glass wall makes the meeting visible from the corridor.
normal.cn: 玻璃隔墙让走廊上的人也能看见会议。

normal.en: A published budget is a glass wall around public money.
normal.cn: 公布的预算，是围着公款的一堵玻璃墙。

normal.en: A transparent excuse is one you can see through, which is why it embarrasses the speaker.
normal.cn: 一眼看穿的借口，正是能被人看透的借口，于是让说话的人难堪。

normal.en: Software calls a change transparent when it is so smooth that nobody notices it.
normal.cn: 软件把改动称为「透明」，是指它顺畅到没人察觉。

normal.en: Transparent lets shapes through; translucent lets only light through.
normal.cn: 「透明的」让形状透出来，「半透明的」只让光透出来。

abstract.en: Opacity protects for a while and then becomes the thing everyone investigates.
abstract.cn: 不透明能保护一阵子，然后就变成所有人都要查的东西。

abstract.en: The same word is praise in government and mockery in an excuse, because both are about being seen.
abstract.cn: 同一个词在政务里是褒义、在借口里是讥讽，因为两者都关乎「被看见」。

abstract.en: A system is transparent when it costs more to hide than to explain.
abstract.cn: 当隐瞒的代价高于解释的代价时，制度就是透明的。

examples.en: The report calls for a transparent system of grants and published criteria.
examples.cn: 报告呼吁建立透明的拨款制度并公布标准。

examples.en: His sudden interest was transparent to everyone at the table.
examples.cn: 他突然表现出的兴趣，在座每个人都看得明白。

examples.en: The coating keeps the screen transparent while blocking most ultraviolet light.
examples.cn: 这层涂层让屏幕保持透明，同时挡住大部分紫外线。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「穿斯帕若」：光「穿」过去，背后的东西就「显」出来了，账目也一样

root: 由拉丁语表示「穿过」的前缀与表示「显现」的动词合成，义为「透过显现」，其分词经法语进入英语。同族有表示「明显的」「外观」的词；形近而表示「泄露、蒸腾」的词出自表示「呼吸」的另一词根。十五世纪进入英语，计算机义为现代新增，首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses split into optics and openness: see-through, honest, traceable process, open government, a see-through excuse, readable intentions, clear accounts, invisible software, and plain truth.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项分为光学与公开两类：透明、诚实、可追踪的流程、政务公开、一眼看穿的借口、可读的意图、清楚的账目、不可见的软件，以及显而易见的道理。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: light passes through the glass wall, and the whole meeting is visible from the corridor.
core.cn: 核心意象：光穿过玻璃隔墙，整个会议在走廊上也看得见。

branches.en: THE GLASS AND THE EXCUSE: literally see-through, then see-through in the mocking sense.
branches.cn: 玻璃与借口：先是字面的看透，再是带讥讽的看透。

branches.en: THE OPEN LEDGER: honesty in conduct and public business laid open.
branches.cn: 敞开的账本：行为上的诚实与公开办理的公共事务。

branches.en: THE TRACEABLE PROCEDURE: steps and accounts that outsiders can check.
branches.cn: 可追踪的程序：外部人能核查的步骤与账目。

branches.en: THE READABLE MIND: intentions and truths that need no explanation.
branches.cn: 可读的心思：无需解释的意图与道理。

branches.en: THE INVISIBLE TOOL: transparency as not getting in the way.
branches.cn: 看不见的工具：以不挡路为「透明」。

intro.en: Transparent is a Latin across-and-appear compound with an adjective ending; the family covers appearance and the quality of openness.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「穿过＋显现」的复合词加形容词尾；词族覆盖「外观」与「公开性」。

latinIntro.en: Latin trans and parere combine in transparere, and the participle transparens supplies the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「穿过」与「显现」合成动词，其分词给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks passage from one side to the other.
items.exampleCN: 它标出从一侧到另一侧的穿行。

items.example: It stands behind apparent and appearance.
items.exampleCN: 它是「明显的」与「外观」背后的词。

items.example: The direct source of the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是该形容词的直接来源。

items.example: Its English form ends in -ent.
items.exampleCN: 其英语形式带形容词词尾。

items.example: It marks the present participle shape.
items.exampleCN: 它标出现在分词的形态。

items.example: It forms transparency.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「透明性」。

items.example: It forms transparently.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「透明地」。

items.example: It forms semi-transparent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「半透明的」。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「透明；公开性」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「透明地」
由表示「一半」的前缀加该形容词构成，义为「半透明的」

definition_zh: 微不足道的；琐碎的；轻微的；（数学）平凡的；浅薄的
definition_en: of little importance or value, or so simple that it needs no special effort
core_image: 会议桌一端堆着修改用词的纸条，另一端那份预算缺口表始终没人翻开
scene: 会议开了半小时，大家还在争表格里一个无关紧要的用词，真正的预算缺口没人提。The committee spent an hour on a trivial wording issue while the budget gap went unmentioned.
sceneCN: 这里指重要性很小、不值得花时间（第 1 个义项：微不足道的）；句意为委员会花一小时争一个无关紧要的用词，预算缺口却无人提及。图中可辨识物件：会议桌、修改用词的纸条、预算缺口表、翻开的文件夹。

pos.zh: 微不足道的；琐碎的；浅薄的
（数学）平凡的；显然的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「琐碎；微不足道的事」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「微不足道地；平凡地」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使显得琐碎；轻描淡写」
由「使显得琐碎」加名词尾构成，义为「淡化；琐碎化」
由拉丁语「三岔路」构成，义为中世纪的三门基础学科
由同一拉丁词的中性复数构成，义为「琐事；冷知识」

senses.title: Of little importance
senses.definition: too small or unimportant to affect the main matter
senses.definitionCN: 太小或不重要，影响不到主要问题
senses.example: The delay was trivial compared with the cost of a wrong decision.
senses.exampleCN: 与错误决策的代价相比，这点延误微不足道。
senses.why: The word's history runs from the crossroads to the common, and then to the common that no longer matters.
senses.whyCN: 这个词的历史从「三岔路口」走到「平常」，再走到「平常到不再重要」。

senses.title: An everyday trifle
senses.definition: a small everyday detail hardly worth attention
senses.definitionCN: 不值得关注的小日常细节
senses.example: They argued about whose turn it was to water the plants, a trivial matter in a busy week.
senses.exampleCN: 他们争该轮到谁浇花，这在忙碌的一周里只是琐事。
senses.why: A matter is trivial when its size, not its difficulty, is the reason to ignore it.
senses.whyCN: 一件事被称为琐事，是因为它小，而不是因为它难。

senses.title: A cost too small to count
senses.definition: an expense so small that it does not change a decision
senses.definitionCN: 小到不会改变决策的支出
senses.example: The extra licence fee is trivial next to the legal risk.
senses.exampleCN: 与法律风险相比，额外的许可费微不足道。
senses.why: Costs are trivial when the decision would be the same without them.
senses.whyCN: 成本在去掉它决策也不变时，就是微不足道的。

senses.title: The obvious solution in mathematics
senses.definition: the simple solution that satisfies the equation without special work, often zero
senses.definitionCN: 无需特别处理即满足方程的简单解，常为零
senses.example: The equation has a trivial solution at zero and two others that matter.
senses.exampleCN: 这个方程有一个位于零的平凡解，另有两个真正重要的解。
senses.why: Mathematics uses the word for the case that gives itself away, which is the technical descendant of commonplace.
senses.whyCN: 数学用它指那个自己送上门的情形，是「平常」这一义的技术后裔。

senses.title: An objection that misses the point
senses.definition: a complaint that does not touch the main question
senses.definitionCN: 没有触及主要问题的抱怨
senses.example: He raised a trivial objection about the font and said nothing about the data.
senses.exampleCN: 他对字体提了个无关紧要的反对，对数据却一言不发。
senses.why: An objection is trivial when it leaves the main claim standing.
senses.whyCN: 反对在主要主张仍然立得住时，就是无关紧要的。

senses.title: Small details used to avoid the issue
senses.definition: minor points brought up to delay or distract
senses.definitionCN: 用细小的点来拖延或转移注意
senses.example: The report drowns in trivial details and never states the cause.
senses.exampleCN: 报告淹没在细枝末节里，始终没说清原因。
senses.why: Details become trivial when they are used to fill the space where the argument should be.
senses.whyCN: 当细节被用来填满本该放论证的位置，它们就成了细枝末节。

senses.title: Shallow talk
senses.definition: conversation without substance or interest
senses.definitionCN: 没有实质或趣味的谈话
senses.example: The party talk was trivial, but it passed the evening.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会上的谈话很浅薄，却也把晚上打发了。
senses.why: Talk without substance earns the word because it leaves nothing behind.
senses.whyCN: 没有实质的谈话得到这个词，因为它什么也没留下。

senses.title: A minor fault
senses.definition: an offence treated as slight rather than serious
senses.definitionCN: 被当作轻微而非严重的过错
senses.example: Under the old rules, a late form was a trivial offence with no penalty.
senses.exampleCN: 按旧规，迟交表格属轻微过失，不受处罚。
senses.why: Law calls a fault trivial when the penalty is lighter than the paperwork.
senses.whyCN: 当处罚比文书手续还轻时，法律就把该过失称为轻微的。

senses.title: Too simple to need comment
senses.definition: so easy in computing or logic that it is not worth explaining
senses.definitionCN: 在计算机或逻辑上简单到不值得解释
senses.example: The remaining case is trivial, so the proof simply says it follows.
senses.exampleCN: 剩下的情形简单到无需说明，证明里只写一句「由此可得」。
senses.why: The technical sense keeps the oldest idea: so common and easy that it needs no remark.
senses.whyCN: 技术义保留了最古老的意思：太寻常、太容易，因而不必再提。

intro.en: Trivial comes from Latin trivialis, belonging to the crossroads, from trivium, a place where three roads meet. Medieval schools called the first three arts the trivium, so the adjective meant belonging to the basic studies, then commonplace, and finally of little importance. The modern sense grew out of that social judgement rather than from the number three.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语中表示「属于三岔路的」形容词，出自表示「三条路交汇处」的名词。中世纪学校把最初三门学科称为「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础学科的」，再变成「平常的」，最后成为「不重要的」。现代义从这种社会判断长出来，而不是从数字「三」直接得来。

items.en: A trivium was a place where three roads met, from tri- three and via road.
items.cn: 这个词指三条路交汇之处，由「三」与「道路」构成。
