items.en: The adjective meant belonging to such a public corner, hence common and ordinary.
items.cn: 该形容词指属于这种人流交汇的公共角落，因此有「平常、普通」之意。

items.en: The first three liberal arts were called the trivium, and trivialis came to mean belonging to basic instruction.
items.cn: 最初三门博雅学科合称「三艺」，形容词于是指「属于基础教学的」。

items.en: English took the word for things common and therefore slight.
items.cn: 英语把这个词用于平常因而轻贱的事物。

items.en: The sense of unimportant hardened, and mathematics adopted it for the obvious case.
items.cn: 「不重要」义渐趋固定，数学又用它指显然的情形。

items.en: Quiz games and computing gave the word new phrases; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 问答游戏与计算机给出新的说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the crossroads root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of smallness. The note also ties trivial to its noun triviality.
note.cn: 第一组共享「三岔路」词根或形近；第二组指其他「小」的说法。这里也把形容词与其名词形式「琐碎」连起来。

entries.definition: The quality of being trivial, or a trivial thing.
entries.definitionCN: 指微不足道的性质，或一件琐事。

entries.definition: In a way that is easy or unimportant.
entries.definitionCN: 指以轻易或不重要的方式。

entries.definition: To make something serious seem trivial.
entries.definitionCN: 指把严肃的事说得微不足道。

entries.definition: The three basic arts of the medieval curriculum.
entries.definitionCN: 指中世纪课程里的三门基础学科。

entries.definition: Small facts and unimportant details.
entries.definitionCN: 指小而无关紧要的事实与细节。

entries.definition: Hard labour or painful effort; it comes from a word for a three-pronged tool, not from the crossroads.
entries.definitionCN: 指艰苦劳作或痛苦努力；出自指三齿工具的词，与三岔路无关。

entries.definition: Too small to matter.
entries.definitionCN: 指小到不值得考虑。

entries.definition: Small and unimportant, often said with a slight reproach.
entries.definitionCN: 指小而不重要，常带轻微责备。

entries.definition: Smaller in size, rank or importance than others.
entries.definitionCN: 指在规模、位次或重要性上较小。

entries.definition: So small that it can be ignored in practice.
entries.definitionCN: 指小到实践中可以忽略。

entries.definition: Small-minded or concerned with small matters.
entries.definitionCN: 指心胸窄或只在意小事。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the crossroads, the basic school subjects, the meeting that argues about wording, and the obvious equation case.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用三岔路口、基础学科、为一个用词争吵的会议，以及显然的方程情形。

normal.en: A crossroads is public and common, and common things soon look small.
normal.cn: 三岔路是公共而平常的，而平常的东西很快就显得微小。

normal.en: The three basic arts were the trivium, so trivial once meant elementary, not worthless.
normal.cn: 三门基础学科合称三艺，所以这个词曾经意为「基础的」，而不是「无价值的」。

normal.en: A trivial solution is the one that offers itself without effort.
normal.cn: 平凡解就是那个不用费力自己送上门的解。

normal.en: A trivial objection changes the font, not the argument.
normal.cn: 无关紧要的反对改的是字体，不是论证。

normal.en: Triviality is what happens when a serious subject is discussed only in small details.
normal.cn: 琐碎化，就是严肃话题只剩细枝末节时发生的事。

abstract.en: Calling something trivial is a way of deciding what will not be looked at.
abstract.cn: 把某事称为微不足道，是在决定什么不必再看。

abstract.en: The crossroads made a word for the common, and the common became a verdict on worth.
abstract.cn: 「三岔路」造出了一个表示「平常」的词，而「平常」又变成了对价值的判决。

abstract.en: Every field keeps a set of trivial cases, and they are the ones that teach the shape of the rest.
abstract.cn: 每个领域都留着一批平凡情形，而正是它们教人看清其余部分的形状。

examples.en: The difference in price is trivial compared with the difference in quality.
examples.cn: 与质量差距相比，价格差距微不足道。

examples.en: Do not waste the meeting on trivial details that the report already covers.
examples.cn: 别把会议浪费在报告里已经写到的细枝末节上。

examples.en: The first case is trivial, so the proof moves straight to the second.
examples.cn: 第一种情形简单到无需说明，所以证明直接转向第二种。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「吹尾偶」：三岔路口人来人往，人人都聊的「小事」，风一「吹」就散了

root: 源于拉丁语中表示「三岔路口」的名词，由「三」与「道路」构成，派生形容词义为「属于三岔路的、平常的」。中世纪把三门基础学科合称三艺，于是又指「基础学科的」，再演变为「平常的」，最后成为「微不足道的」。数学「平凡解」义为十九世纪后的技术引申；各短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from the crossroads to the equation: unimportant, an everyday trifle, a negligible cost, the obvious mathematical case, a pointless objection, distracting details, shallow talk, a slight fault, and the simple case that needs no comment.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从三岔路走到方程：不重要、日常琐事、可忽略的成本、数学的显然情形、无的放矢的反对、转移注意的细节、浅薄的闲谈、轻微过失，以及无需说明的简单情形。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one end of the table is covered with notes about wording, while the budget sheet stays shut.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌子一端堆满改词的纸条，另一端的预算表始终没有翻开。

branches.en: THE SMALL AMOUNT: importance and cost measured and found tiny.
branches.cn: 微小的分量：重要性与成本一量就小。

branches.en: THE TRIFLE AND THE DISTRACTION: small items, and small items used to avoid the point.
branches.cn: 琐事与分神：小东西，以及被用来回避要点的小东西。

branches.en: THE EASY CASE: the solution or case that offers itself.
branches.cn: 轻易的情形：自己送上门的解或情形。

branches.en: THE LIGHT COMPLAINT: an objection or fault too slight to matter.
branches.cn: 轻微的抱怨：轻到不必计较的反对或过失。

branches.en: THE SHALLOW TALK: conversation without substance.
branches.cn: 浅薄的谈话：没有实质的闲聊。

intro.en: Trivial is a crossroads noun with an adjective ending; the family covers trivia, the three basic arts, and the act of making something seem small.
intro.cn: 这个词是「三岔路」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖冷知识、三门基础学科，以及「把某事说得微不足道」的动作。

latinIntro.en: Latin tri- and via build trivium, and the derived adjective trivialis supplies the English word and its whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「三」与「道路」构成表示「三岔路」的名词，派生形容词给出英语词及其整个词族。

items.example: It marks the meeting of three roads.
items.exampleCN: 它标出三条路的交汇。

items.example: It is also the source of English via.
items.exampleCN: 它也是英语「经由」的来源。

items.example: The noun behind the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族背后的名词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把该词标为形容词。

items.example: It forms triviality.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「琐碎」。

items.example: It forms trivialize.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「使显得琐碎」。

items.example: The plural keeps the idea of many small things.
items.exampleCN: 复数保留了「许多小东西」的意思。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「琐碎；琐事」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「微不足道地」
由该形容词加动词尾构成，义为「使显得琐碎」
由「使显得琐碎」加名词尾构成，义为「淡化；琐碎化」
由拉丁语「三岔路」构成，义为中世纪三门基础学科

definition_zh: 根本的；潜在的；底层的；隐含的；下伏的；作为基础的
definition_en: lying beneath something visible, and therefore basic, hidden or not yet stated
core_image: 销售报表最上面一页是逐月下滑的订单曲线，翻到最后一页才看见续约率一路走低
scene: 销售报表上订单逐月下滑，真正的原因却藏在最后一页的客户续约率里。The report traced the drop in orders to an underlying loss of long-term customers.
sceneCN: 这里指藏在表象之下、起决定作用的根本原因（第 1 个义项：表象之下的根本原因）；句意为报告把订单下滑归因于潜在的长期客户流失。图中可辨识物件：销售报表、订单曲线、续约率折线、最后一页。

pos.zh: 根本的；潜在的；底层的；隐含的
（地质）下伏的；在下面的

derivatives.zh: 由表示「在下」的成分与表示「躺、位于」的成分复合而成，义为「位于……之下；是……的基础」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「在根本上；在底层」
由表示「在下」的成分与另一个表示「铺放」的动词复合而成，义为「铺在下面」，与动词原形不同
同上，作名词义为「衬垫物」

senses.title: The cause beneath the symptom
senses.definition: the real cause that produces what is visible on the surface
senses.definitionCN: 产生表面可见现象的真正原因
senses.example: Doctors looked for an underlying cause rather than treating each symptom.
senses.exampleCN: 医生寻找根本原因，而不是逐个处理症状。
senses.why: The word is built from lying under, so the cause is pictured as a layer beneath the symptom.
senses.whyCN: 这个词由「躺在下面」构成，于是原因被画成症状之下的一层。

senses.title: An assumption not stated
senses.definition: a belief that supports an argument without being spoken
senses.definitionCN: 支撑论证却未被说出口的信念
senses.example: The model's underlying assumption is that prices always reflect all information.
senses.exampleCN: 这个模型的潜在假设是价格总能反映全部信息。
senses.why: What lies under a claim does not show, and that is exactly why it needs naming.
senses.whyCN: 托在主张之下的东西不会自己显露，正因如此才需要被点出来。

senses.title: The basic structure
senses.definition: the framework on which the visible parts rest
senses.definitionCN: 可见部分所依托的框架
senses.example: The underlying structure of the language is simpler than its surface patterns.
senses.exampleCN: 这种语言的底层结构比它的表层模式简单。
senses.why: A structure is underlying when removing it would collapse what stands on it.
senses.whyCN: 当抽掉它上面的东西就会塌，这个结构就是底层的。

senses.title: The asset behind a security
senses.definition: the asset on which a derivative or security is based
senses.definitionCN: 衍生工具或证券所依托的资产
senses.example: When the underlying asset falls, the contract loses value.
senses.exampleCN: 标的资产下跌时，合约就贬值。
senses.why: Finance borrowed the physical image: something real lies under the paper.
senses.whyCN: 金融借用了这个实物意象：纸张之下压着真东西。

senses.title: A condition already present
senses.definition: a medical condition that existed before the current illness
senses.definitionCN: 在当前疾病之前就已存在的身体状况
senses.example: The fever was mild, but the underlying condition made it dangerous.
senses.exampleCN: 发烧本身不重，但基础疾病让它变得危险。
senses.why: Medicine says a condition is underlying when it was there before the illness being treated.
senses.whyCN: 医学把在正在治疗的疾病之前就已存在的状况称为基础疾病。

senses.title: A trend beneath short-term noise
senses.titleCN: 短期波动之下的潜在趋势
senses.definition: a long-run direction visible only under the fluctuations
senses.definitionCN: 只有在波动之下才看得出的长期方向
senses.example: Monthly sales jump about, but the underlying trend is flat.
senses.exampleCN: 月度销量起伏不定，潜在趋势却是平的。
senses.why: The trend is what remains after the monthly noise is averaged away.
senses.whyCN: 把月度噪声平均掉之后剩下的，就是潜在趋势。

senses.title: Deeper meaning
senses.definition: the meaning below the literal words
senses.definitionCN: 字面之下的含义
senses.example: The underlying meaning of the letter is a request for help.
senses.exampleCN: 这封信的深层含义是请求帮助。
senses.why: Meaning can have layers too: the sentence on the surface, the request underneath.
senses.whyCN: 含义也能分层：表层是一句话，底下是一个请求。

senses.title: A risk not yet visible
senses.definition: a danger that exists but has not yet shown itself
senses.definitionCN: 已经存在却尚未暴露的危险
senses.example: The audit found an underlying risk in the payment system.
senses.exampleCN: 审计在支付系统中发现一处潜在风险。
senses.why: A risk is underlying while it exists in the system but has not yet produced an event.
senses.whyCN: 当风险存在于系统中却尚未酿成事件时，它就是潜在的。

senses.title: The rock beneath the soil
senses.definition: the layer of rock below the surface material
senses.definitionCN: 地表物质之下的岩层
senses.example: The drill reached the underlying rock at twelve metres.
senses.exampleCN: 钻机在十二米处碰到了下伏岩层。
senses.why: This is the plainest layer sense, and the figurative uses all borrow its picture.
senses.whyCN: 这是最直白的「层」义，所有比喻用法都借用这幅画面。

intro.en: Underlying is an English compound of under and lie, with the ordinary meaning of something resting beneath another thing. English built it from native elements rather than from Latin, and the figurative senses of cause, assumption and trend all keep the physical picture of a layer underneath.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族成分「在下」与「躺卧」的复合，本义指某物躺在另一物之下。它由本族语素构成，而非来自拉丁语；原因、假设、趋势等引申义都保留「下面一层」的实物画面。

items.en: Under named a position below something, and it also carried the idea of submission.
items.cn: 这个词表示在某物之下的位置，也带有「受制于」的意思。

items.en: Licgan meant to lie down or rest, and it survives as the verb lie in modern English.
items.cn: 这个词意为躺下、安放，在现代英语里保存为动词「躺」。

items.en: The compound named what lies beneath a surface, first in the physical sense.
items.cn: 这个复合词指位于表面之下者，最初是实物义。

items.en: The participle form came to modify causes, structures and trends rather than visible objects.
items.cn: 这一分词形式后来修饰原因、结构与趋势，而不再只修饰可见物体。

items.en: Markets gave it the fixed phrase underlying asset, meaning the thing beneath a contract.
items.cn: 金融市场给出固定说法「标的资产」，指合约之下的那件东西。

items.en: Both fields kept the literal layer sense; the first date of each technical use is uncertain.
items.cn: 地质与医学都保留了字面的「层」义；两种技术用法首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group looks close and shares the lying-under picture; the second group names other kinds of depth. Several look-alikes come from different verbs and must not be confused with this one.
note.cn: 第一组形近且共享「躺在下面」的画面；第二组指其他「深一层」的说法。几个形近词出自不同动词，不可与它混为一谈。

entries.definition: To be the basis of something, or to lie beneath it.
entries.definitionCN: 指构成某物的基础，或位于其下。

entries.definition: At the level of what lies beneath.
entries.definitionCN: 指在底层那个层面。

entries.definition: To lay something under another thing, as a carpet under a floor covering; it uses the verb lay, not lie.
entries.definitionCN: 指把某物铺在另一物之下，如地毯下的衬垫；用的是「铺放」动词，而非「躺卧」动词。

entries.definition: To draw a line under words, or to emphasize.
entries.definitionCN: 指在文字下画线，或加以强调。

entries.definition: To weaken gradually, from digging a mine under a wall.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐削弱，源自在地基下挖坑道。

entries.definition: A subordinate person; the ending is a diminutive, not a form of lie.
entries.definitionCN: 指下属；词尾是表小的成分，与「躺卧」无关。

entries.definition: Serving as the base on which everything else rests, often said of principles.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为其余一切所依托的基础，常用于原则。

entries.definition: Present but not stated openly.
entries.definitionCN: 指存在却未被公开说出。

entries.definition: Existing but not yet active or visible.
entries.definitionCN: 指已存在但尚未活动或显现。

entries.definition: Belonging to the base, used mostly in biology and geology.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于底部的，多用于生物学与地质学。

entries.definition: The origin from which something grows, used figuratively of causes.
entries.definitionCN: 指事物生长的根源，比喻原因。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the bottom sheet of the report, the layer under paint, the foundation under a wall and the fault line under a city.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用报表最后一页、油漆下面的一层、墙下的地基与城市下的断层。

normal.en: Turn the report to its last page: the underlying cause is usually printed there.
normal.cn: 把报表翻到最后一页：根本原因通常印在那里。

normal.en: The pattern you see is paint; the underlying structure is the wall.
normal.cn: 你看见的花纹是油漆，底层结构是那面墙。

normal.en: A house rests on what you never see, and so does an argument.
normal.cn: 房子靠着你看不见的部分，论证也一样。

normal.en: An underlying assumption is a floor nobody has inspected.
normal.cn: 潜在假设是一块没人检查过的地板。

normal.en: Underlie means to lie under; underlay means to lay something under, and the two verbs differ.
normal.cn: 「位于其下」与「铺在其下」是两个不同的动词。

abstract.en: Every visible pattern is a compromise with something underneath it.
abstract.cn: 每个看得见的模式，都是与其下之物达成的妥协。

abstract.en: The word is a geological gift to argument: causes are layers too.
abstract.cn: 这个词是地质学送给论证的礼物：原因也是分层的。

abstract.en: What is underlying is not hidden on purpose; it simply has no surface of its own.
abstract.cn: 「底层的」并非有意躲藏，它只是没有自己的表面。

examples.en: The underlying cause of the shortage was a five-year decline in storage capacity.
examples.cn: 短缺的根本原因是储存能力连续五年下降。

examples.en: Any change to the underlying asset changes the value of the contract.
examples.cn: 标的资产一旦变动，合约价值随之改变。

examples.en: The underlying rock here is older than the valley itself.
examples.cn: 这里的下伏岩层比河谷本身还要古老。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「安德莱应」：报表上面那层是数字，底下那层才是原「因」，得把纸翻过去看

root: 英语本族复合词，由表示「在下」与表示「躺、位于」的两个古英语成分加上分词词尾构成。本义为「躺在下面」，引申为「根本的、潜在的、底层的」。金融的「标的资产」、医学的「基础疾病」、地质的「下伏岩层」都在这幅画面上各取一层；各技术用法首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses share one picture of a lower layer: cause, assumption, structure, the asset behind a contract, a pre-existing illness, trend under noise, deeper meaning, hidden risk, and rock under soil.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项共享「下面一层」的同一幅画：原因、假设、结构、合约背后的资产、原有的疾病、波动下的趋势、深层含义、隐藏的风险，以及表土下的岩层。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last page of the report carries the line nobody read first.
core.cn: 核心意象：报表最后一页写着没人先去看的那一行。

branches.en: THE FOUNDATION: the cause and the structure on which the visible rests.
branches.cn: 地基：原因与结构，托住可见的部分。

branches.en: THE CONTRACT'S FLOOR: an unstated assumption, and the asset beneath a security.
branches.cn: 合约的地板：未说出的假设，以及证券之下的资产。

branches.en: THE QUIET CONDITION: an existing illness and a risk not yet visible.
branches.cn: 沉默的状况：已存在的疾病与尚未显现的风险。

branches.en: THE SIGNAL UNDER NOISE: a long trend and a deeper meaning.
branches.cn: 噪声下的信号：长期趋势与深层含义。

branches.en: THE ROCK BELOW: the literal layer that gives the picture.
branches.cn: 下面的岩石：给出画面的字面那一层。

intro.en: Underlying is a native English compound, not a Latin borrowing, so its parts are the ordinary words under and lie.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族复合词，不是拉丁语借词，所以构件就是普通的「在下」与「躺卧」。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin root here; the layer picture comes from two Old English words joined together.
latinIntro.cn: 这里没有拉丁词根；「分层」的画面来自两个古英语词的组合。

items.example: It supplies the lower position.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「较低的位置」。

items.example: It supplies the resting object.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「躺着的事物」。

items.example: The older form of the modern verb.
items.exampleCN: 这是现代动词的更早形式。

items.example: It is the verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是形容词背后的动词。

items.example: It turns the verb into a describing word.
items.exampleCN: 它把动词变成描述性的词。

items.example: It forms underlyingly.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「在根本上」。

items.example: A different verb, not a form of lie.
items.exampleCN: 这是另一个动词，不是「躺卧」的形式。

items.example: It looks close but belongs to line.
items.exampleCN: 它形近，却属于「线」这一支。

senses.title: The same everywhere
senses.definition: identical in all places or in all cases
senses.definitionCN: 在所有地方或情形中都相同
senses.example: The tiles are uniform in size, so the floor looks even.
senses.exampleCN: 瓷砖尺寸一致，地面看上去很平整。
senses.why: The Latin parts mean one form, and one form repeated is exactly what this sense describes.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语构件意为「一个形状」，同一个形状反复出现，正是这一义项所描述的。

senses.title: A single standard for all
senses.definition: one rule or measure applied to everyone without exception
senses.definitionCN: 对所有人无例外地适用同一规则或尺度
senses.example: The agency set a uniform standard for labelling across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 该机构为全区设定了统一的标签标准。
senses.why: A standard becomes uniform when local exceptions are removed, which is a political act rather than a physical one.
senses.whyCN: 当地方例外被取消，标准才变得「统一」，这是政治动作而非物理动作。

senses.title: Steady in rate
senses.definition: moving or changing at an unchanging rate
senses.definitionCN: 以不变的速率移动或变化
senses.example: The trolley moved at a uniform speed along the straight track.
senses.exampleCN: 小车沿直线轨道匀速前进。
senses.why: Time and distance are matched step for step, so the rate is one form too.
senses.whyCN: 时间与距离一步步对应，速率也就成了同一个形状。

senses.title: The clothing of a group
senses.definition: the set of clothes that members of a group are required to wear
senses.definitionCN: 某一群体成员必须穿着的整套服装
senses.example: Nurses in uniform were asked to identify themselves at the entrance.
senses.exampleCN: 穿制服的护士被要求在入口处表明身份。
senses.why: The clothing sense follows from one form worn by many, and the noun keeps the same shape as the adjective.
senses.whyCN: 服装义由「许多人穿同一个样式」而来，名词与形容词同形。

senses.title: Rules with no exceptions
senses.definition: rules applied in the same way to every case
senses.definitionCN: 对每一情形都以同样方式适用的规则
senses.example: The ban is uniform, so no club can claim an exemption.
senses.exampleCN: 禁令一视同仁，任何俱乐部都不能声称豁免。
senses.why: A rule is uniform when the same words bind every case, including the ones the drafters dislike.
senses.whyCN: 当同样的条文约束每一情形、包括起草者不喜欢的情形，规则才是统一的。

senses.title: Evenly spread
senses.definition: spread evenly, with no concentration in one place
senses.definitionCN: 分布平均，不在某处聚集
senses.example: The seeds were sown at a uniform density across the plot.
senses.exampleCN: 种子在整个地块以均匀密度播下。
senses.why: Distribution without lumps is another version of one form repeated.
senses.whyCN: 没有团块的分布，是「同一形状重复」的另一个版本。

senses.title: The same temperature throughout
senses.definition: having one temperature in every part
senses.definitionCN: 每个部分的温度都一样
senses.example: A uniform temperature is needed before the sample can be weighed.
senses.exampleCN: 称量样品前需要各处温度相同。
senses.why: Heat spreads until every part reads the same number, which is sameness made measurable.
senses.whyCN: 热一直扩散到各处读数相同，这就是被量出来的「一致」。

senses.title: A field of equal value
senses.definition: in physics, a field whose strength and direction are the same at every point
senses.definitionCN: 物理学中指各点强度与方向都相同的场
senses.example: In a uniform electric field the force on a charge is constant.
senses.exampleCN: 在均匀电场中，电荷所受的力是恒定的。
senses.why: Physics states the sameness point by point: same strength, same direction, everywhere.
senses.whyCN: 物理把「相同」逐点写明：处处同强度、同方向。

intro.en: Uniform joins Latin unus, one, and forma, form: one form. French used uniforme for clothing and for consistency, and English took both. The noun and the adjective still share one shape, which is fitting for a word about having a single shape.
intro.cn: 这个词由拉丁语 unus「一」与 forma「形状」构成，意为「一个形状」。法语用它指服装与一致性，英语把两者都吸收进来。名词与形容词至今同形，这对一个讲「只有一种形状」的词来说倒也贴切。

items.en: Unus meant one, and it also stands behind unity and union.
items.cn: 这个词意为「一」，也是「统一」与「联合」背后的词。

items.en: Forma meant shape or mould, and it gives form, reform and conform.
items.cn: 这个词意为形状或模子，给出「形式」「改造」「符合」等词。

items.en: The compound meant having one form, and it described things that do not vary.
items.cn: 这个复合词意为「只有一种形状」，形容不变化的事物。

items.en: French used it for both steady things and the dress of a body of men.
items.cn: 法语既用它指稳定不变之物，也指一支队伍的着装。

items.en: English took the adjective first, then the noun for military and school dress.
items.cn: 英语先吸收形容词，后吸收指军警与学校服装的名词。

items.en: Physics, statistics and public rules each gave it fixed phrases; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 物理、统计与公共规则各自给出固定说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the one-form root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of sameness. The note also separates uniform from unify, which looks similar but comes from a different Latin verb.
note.cn: 第一组共享「一个形状」词根或形近；第二组指其他「相同」的说法。这里也把「统一的」与形近但异源的「使成一体」分开。

entries.definition: The quality of being the same throughout.
entries.definitionCN: 指各处相同的性质。

entries.definition: In the same way everywhere, or evenly.
entries.definitionCN: 指处处相同或均匀地。

entries.definition: Wearing an official uniform.
entries.definitionCN: 指穿着制服的。

entries.definition: To shape again, hence to improve a system; it shares the form root, not the one.
entries.definitionCN: 指重新塑形，因而改进制度；共享「形状」词根而非「一」。

entries.definition: To make into one; it uses the Latin verb for making, not the word for form.
entries.definitionCN: 指使成为一体；用的是拉丁语「做」的动词，而非「形状」。

entries.definition: A one-horned animal; the second part means horn.
entries.definitionCN: 指独角的动物；后半意为「角」。

entries.definition: Behaving or appearing in the same way over time.
entries.definitionCN: 指随时间保持同样的表现或样子。

entries.definition: Exactly the same in every detail.
entries.definitionCN: 指每个细节都完全相同。

entries.definition: Flat, level or regular, with no bumps in space or time.
entries.definitionCN: 指平坦、均匀，在空间或时间上没有起伏。

entries.definition: Made of parts of the same kind.
entries.definitionCN: 指由同类部分构成。

entries.definition: Fixed by authority and used as the measure for others.
entries.definitionCN: 指由权威固定、用作衡量他物的尺度。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the school clothing, the factory standard, the steady trolley and the even field.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用校服、工厂标准、匀速小车与均匀场。

normal.en: One form worn by a thousand people is called a uniform.
normal.cn: 同一个样式被一千个人穿上，就叫制服。

normal.en: A uniform standard is one ruler used on every desk.
normal.cn: 统一标准就是每张桌上都用同一把尺。

normal.en: Uniform speed means the speedometer needle never moves.
normal.cn: 匀速就是速度表的指针一直不动。

normal.en: Seed sown evenly gives a uniform field of green.
normal.cn: 种子撒得匀，长出来就是一片均匀的绿。

normal.en: Uniform and unify look alike, but one is about one shape and the other about making one.
normal.cn: 「统一的」与「使成一体」形近，一个说「一个形状」，一个说「做成一体」。

abstract.en: Uniformity is restful to look at and dangerous to think in.
abstract.cn: 统一看上去让人安心，用来思考却危险。

abstract.en: Every uniform hides a decision about who does not fit it.
abstract.cn: 每套制服背后，都藏着一个关于「谁穿不进去」的决定。

abstract.en: Nature is uniform enough to be studied and varied enough to be interesting.
abstract.cn: 自然足够统一，所以能被研究；也足够多样，所以有趣。

examples.en: The ministry issued a uniform procedure for all regional offices.
examples.cn: 该部门为所有地区办事处发布了统一流程。

examples.en: He was still in uniform when the call came at midnight.
examples.cn: 午夜电话来时，他仍穿着制服。

examples.en: Water heats slowly because the pan does not keep a uniform temperature.
examples.cn: 水热得慢，因为锅无法保持各处温度相同。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「优尼佛姆」：同一个「形状」套在所有人身上，就是制服，也是统一

root: 由拉丁语表示「一」的数词与表示「形状」的名词合成，义为「只有一种形状的」，经法语进入英语。同族有表示「一致性」「一致地」「穿制服的」的词；形近而表示「使成一体」的词出自表示「做」的另一动词，表示「独角兽」的词后半意为「角」。十六世纪进入英语；各技术短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses share one form: sameness everywhere, one standard, steady rate, official clothing, rules without exceptions, even spread, even temperature, and a field of equal value.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项共享「一个形状」：处处相同、统一标准、匀速、制服、无例外规则、均匀分布、温度一致与均匀场。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a row of students in identical coats, down to the pocket and the cuff.
core.cn: 核心意象：一排学生穿着完全相同的外套，连口袋与袖口都一样。

branches.en: THE SAME IN EVERY CASE: appearance that repeats and rules that admit no exception.
branches.cn: 每种情形都相同：重复的外观与不容例外的规则。

branches.en: THE SINGLE MEASURE: one standard, and one unvarying rate.
branches.cn: 单一的尺度：一个标准与一个不变的速率。

branches.en: THE GROUP'S CLOTHING: one form worn by many bodies.
branches.cn: 群体的衣服：同一个样式穿在许多身体上。

branches.en: THE EVEN SURFACE: density and temperature spread without lumps.
branches.cn: 平顺的表面：密度与温度分布没有团块。

branches.en: THE FIELD OF EQUAL VALUE: sameness extended to every point in space.
branches.cn: 等值的场：把「相同」推到空间中的每一点。

intro.en: Uniform is two Latin words joined; its family covers the standard, the clothing and the adverb of evenness.
intro.cn: 这个词由两个拉丁词合成；词族覆盖标准、服装与表示「均匀」的副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin unus and forma combine in uniformis, and French passes the compound to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「一」与「形状」合成 uniformis，法语把这个复合词传给英语。

definition_en: being the only one of its kind, or having a quality that no other thing shares

sceneCN: 这里指仅此一个、别处没有相同者（第 1 个义项：独一无二的）；句意为每座火山都有一套独特的火山灰分层，别处找不到相同的。图中可辨识物件：矿石、单独抽屉、纹理标签、整批样本箱。

（少用）独一无二的人或物

senses.title: The only one of its kind
senses.definition: existing as the only example of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 作为同类中唯一的例子而存在
senses.example: The manuscript is unique, and no copy of it survives.
senses.exampleCN: 这份手稿独一无二，没有任何副本留存。
senses.why: The Latin word for one is the whole basis; uniqueness is being one without a second.
senses.whyCN: 「一」这个拉丁词就是全部根据：独一无二，就是只有一个而没有第二个。

senses.title: Found only in one place
senses.definition: existing in one place and nowhere else
senses.definitionCN: 只存在于一处而不见于他处
senses.example: This orchid is unique to the island's northern slopes.
senses.exampleCN: 这种兰花是该岛北坡特有的。
senses.why: Location makes uniqueness easy to test: look elsewhere and find nothing.
senses.whyCN: 位置让「唯一」容易检验：到别处找，什么也找不到。

senses.title: A code with no duplicate
senses.definition: a label or number that no other item in the system shares
senses.definitionCN: 系统中没有其他项目重复使用的标签或编号
senses.example: Every account gets a unique identifier that never changes.
senses.exampleCN: 每个账户都获得一个永不变更的唯一标识。
senses.why: Computer systems need the guarantee, not the poetry: one code, one item.
senses.whyCN: 计算机系统要的是保证而非诗意：一个编码只对应一个项目。

senses.title: An opportunity that will not return
senses.definition: a chance unlikely to come again
senses.definitionCN: 不太可能再来的机会
senses.example: The fellowship is a unique opportunity for early researchers.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金对年轻研究者是难得的机会。
senses.why: A chance is called unique when the calendar offers no second date for it.
senses.whyCN: 当日历上排不出第二个日期，这个机会就被称为难得。

senses.title: A style of one's own
senses.definition: a way of working or speaking that others do not share
senses.definitionCN: 他人所没有的工作或说话方式
senses.example: Her photographs have a unique way of framing a crowd.
senses.exampleCN: 她的照片有一种独特的取景人群的方式。
senses.why: A manner repeated by nobody else is unique in the way a signature is.
senses.whyCN: 无人重复的做法是独特的，就像签名一样。

senses.title: The single solution
senses.definition: the one solution that satisfies a problem
senses.definitionCN: 满足某一问题的唯一解
senses.example: With these two conditions the equation has a unique solution.
senses.exampleCN: 加上这两个条件，方程只有唯一解。
senses.why: Mathematics borrows the word to make a strong claim: existence plus oneness.
senses.whyCN: 数学借用这个词作出强断言：既存在，又只有一个。

senses.title: A feature no rival has
senses.definition: an advantage that only this product or person offers
senses.definitionCN: 只有这个产品或这个人具备的优势
senses.example: The plant's unique selling point is that it grows in salt water.
senses.exampleCN: 这种植物的独特卖点是能在咸水中生长。
senses.why: Markets name the feature no rival copies, and uniqueness becomes an argument for price.
senses.whyCN: 市场把对手无法复制的特点点出来，「唯一」于是成了定价的理由。

senses.title: A pattern that never repeats
senses.definition: a set of marks that no other sample reproduces
senses.definitionCN: 没有其他样本能复现的一组纹路
senses.example: Fingerprints are unique even between identical twins.
senses.exampleCN: 连完全相同的双胞胎之间，指纹也不重复。
senses.why: The pattern is unique because no second sample can reproduce it, not because it is beautiful.
senses.whyCN: 图案之所以独一无二，是因为没有第二个样本能复现，而不是因为它好看。

senses.title: Informal: very unusual
senses.definition: in relaxed speech, merely remarkable rather than strictly the only one
senses.definitionCN: 在口语里只表示「很特别」，并非严格意义上的「唯一」
senses.example: The café has a unique atmosphere, though other places are similar.
senses.exampleCN: 这家咖啡馆气氛特别，尽管别处也有类似的。
senses.why: Strict usage says one of a kind; loose usage says merely remarkable, and both are now common.
senses.whyCN: 严格用法要求「仅此一个」，宽松用法只表示「很特别」，两种现在都很常见。

intro.en: Unique comes from Latin unicus, one of a kind, from unus, one, through French unique. English took it in the sixteenth century for things that exist only once, and relaxed speech later weakened it to mean merely remarkable.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 unicus「独一的」，出自 unus「一」，经法语进入英语。十六世纪用于只存在一次的事物；后来的口语把它削弱为「很特别」的意思。

items.en: Unus meant one, and it supplies union, unity and unit as well.
items.cn: 这个词意为「一」，也提供「联合」「统一」「单位」等词。

items.en: The adjective meant single or one of a kind, with no second example.
items.cn: 该形容词意为「单一的、独一的」，没有第二个例子。

items.en: French kept the strong sense of oneness when the word entered discussion of style and character.
items.cn: 法语在该词进入风格与性格的讨论时，保留了强烈的「唯一」义。

items.en: English applied it to manuscripts, species and personal manners.
items.cn: 英语把它用于手稿、物种与个人举止。

items.en: Computing adopted it for identifiers that cannot repeat.
items.cn: 计算机领域把它用于不可重复的标识。

items.en: Everyday speech extended it to anything striking; the exact date of that weakening is uncertain.
items.cn: 日常口语把它扩展到一切引人注目之物；这一弱化的确切年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the one root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of distinctness. The note also sets unique against widespread, its natural opposite in describing how far something reaches.
note.cn: 第一组共享「一」词根或形近；第二组指其他「独特」的说法。这里也把「独一无二的」与它的自然反义「分布广泛的」对照，二者说的正是「延伸得多远」。

entries.definition: In a way that only one thing does.
entries.definitionCN: 指以唯有其一的方式。

entries.definition: The state of having no second example.
entries.definitionCN: 指没有第二个例子的状态。

entries.definition: One thing taken as a measure or a member.
entries.definitionCN: 指作为计量或成员的一个单位。

entries.definition: A one-horned creature; the second part means horn.
entries.definitionCN: 指独角的生物；后半意为「角」。

entries.definition: Sounding together; the second part means sound.
entries.definitionCN: 指同时发声；后半意为「声音」。

entries.definition: Found over a large area or among many people; the opposite direction of reach.
entries.definitionCN: 指分布在大范围或许多人之中的；说的是延伸方向的另一端。

entries.definition: One of a kind, and in grammar, referring to one.
entries.definitionCN: 指独一的；语法上指单数。

entries.definition: The only one, often with legal or formal force.
entries.definitionCN: 指唯一的，常带法律或正式意味。

entries.definition: Having no equal in quality.
entries.definitionCN: 指质量上无可匹敌的。

entries.definition: Marking something out from others rather than being the only one.
entries.definitionCN: 指使某物区别于其他，而不是「唯一」。

entries.definition: Unusually good or unusual, not necessarily unique.
entries.definitionCN: 指异常出色或罕见，但不一定是唯一的。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the single drawer, the island orchid, the account code and the fingerprint.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用单独抽屉、岛上兰花、账户编码与指纹。

normal.en: A unique thing has no second copy, so there is nothing to compare it with.
normal.cn: 独一无二之物没有副本，因此无从比较。

normal.en: An identifier is unique when no other item answers to it.
normal.cn: 当没有别的项目应答同一个编码时，它就是唯一标识。

normal.en: A unique opportunity is one that will not wait for you.
normal.cn: 难得的机会，是不会在原地等你的那一个。

normal.en: Fingerprints are the everyday proof that uniqueness is real.
normal.cn: 指纹是「独一无二确实存在」的日常证据。

normal.en: Unique is the opposite of widespread: one is one place, the other is every place.
normal.cn: 「独一无二」与「分布广泛」相反：一个只在一点，一个遍布各处。

abstract.en: Uniqueness is a claim about the world, and it needs a world to check it against.
abstract.cn: 「独一无二」是关于世界的断言，也需要世界来核对。

abstract.en: A system full of unique identifiers can still be full of duplicate people.
abstract.cn: 一个充满唯一编码的系统，仍可能装满重复的人。

abstract.en: The word is strongest when it is a fact and weakest when it is praise.
abstract.cn: 这个词在陈述事实时最有力，在充当赞美时最虚弱。

examples.en: The archive holds a unique set of letters from the period.
examples.cn: 该档案馆藏有一批那个时期独一无二的书信。

examples.en: This species is unique to two valleys in the south.
examples.cn: 这个物种只存在于南方的两条河谷。

examples.en: Give each sample a unique label before it leaves the bench.
examples.cn: 每份样品离开工作台前，都贴上一个唯一标签。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「优尼扣」：整批里只此一份，像衣服上唯一的一颗「扣」子，掉了就再找不到

root: 源于拉丁语表示「一」的数词，其形容词义为「独一的」，经法语进入英语。同族有表示「单位」「独特性」「唯一地」的词；形近的「独角兽」后半意为「角」，「齐声」后半意为「声音」。十六世纪进入英语；口语弱化义的确切年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses run from strict oneness to loose praise: one of a kind, local only, a unique code, a rare chance, a personal style, the single solution, a selling point, an unrepeatable pattern, and the weakened everyday use.
sensesIntro.cn: 九个义项从严守「唯一」走到宽松赞美：仅此一个、某地特有、唯一编码、难得机会、个人风格、唯一解、独特卖点、不可复现的图案，以及被弱化的日常用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the drawer with a single labelled stone, and a note that no second one shares its grain.
core.cn: 核心意象：单独抽屉里那块贴标签的矿石，旁边注明整批没有第二块同样的纹理。

branches.en: THE ABSENT SECOND: strict uniqueness, from manuscripts to fingerprints.
branches.cn: 缺席的第二个：从手稿到指纹的严格唯一。

branches.en: THE LOCAL ADVANTAGE: found only here, or offered only by this one.
branches.cn: 本地的优势：只在这里出现，或只由这一方提供。

branches.en: THE SINGLE ANSWER: one code and one solution, guaranteed rather than admired.
branches.cn: 唯一的答案：一个编码、一个解，是保证而非赞美。

branches.en: THE REMARKABLE: a chance that will not return, and the loosened everyday sense.
branches.cn: 引人注目之处：不会再来的机会，以及被放宽的日常义。

branches.en: THE PERSONAL MANNER: a style no one else repeats.
branches.cn: 个人的做法：无人重复的风格。

intro.en: Unique is a Latin one word with an adjective ending; its family covers unity, the adverb and the technical compound.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「一」加形容词尾；词族覆盖「统一」、副词与技术复合词。

latinIntro.en: Latin unus and its derivative unicus carry the whole idea; French supplies the shape English adopted.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语「一」及其派生「独一的」承担全部意思；法语提供英语采用的形态。

items.example: The root of the whole family.
items.exampleCN: 这是整个词族的根。

items.example: It gives the English adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: The form the word took through French.
items.exampleCN: 这是它经法语形成的形态。

items.example: It appears in unit, union and unison.
items.exampleCN: 它见于「单位」「联合」「齐声」。

items.example: It forms uniqueness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「独特性」。

items.example: It forms uniquely.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「唯一地」。

items.example: It forms non-unique.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「不唯一的」。

items.example: It forms the technical phrase unique identifier.
items.exampleCN: 它与该形容词构成「唯一标识」。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「独特性」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「唯一地」
由否定前缀加该形容词构成，义为「不唯一的」
由该形容词与表示标识的名词构成，义为「唯一标识」

definition_zh: 分布广泛的；普遍存在的；广泛使用的；大范围的
definition_en: existing, happening or believed over a large area or among many people
core_image: 县城一条街从菜摊到早点铺，每张桌上都贴着同一个收款码
scene: 县城的菜摊、公交和早点铺都贴着同一个收款码，用手机付钱已经成了日常。Mobile payment is now widespread even in small county markets.
sceneCN: 这里指在很大范围内普遍存在（第 1 个义项：分布广泛的）；句意为手机支付如今连小县城市场里也普遍使用。图中可辨识物件：菜摊、早点铺、收款码、公交车、手机。

pos.zh: 分布广泛的；普遍存在的；广泛使用的

derivatives.zh: 复合词的前一成分，义为「宽的；广泛的」
由前一成分加副词尾构成，义为「广泛地」
由前一成分加动词尾构成，义为「加宽；扩大」
复合词的后一成分，义为「散布；传播」

senses.title: Found over a large area
senses.definition: present across a large area rather than in one place
senses.definitionCN: 存在于广大地区而不是某一处
senses.example: The fungus is widespread in damp forests across the region.
senses.exampleCN: 这种真菌在该地区潮湿的森林里分布广泛。
senses.why: The first part of the compound means broad and the second means scattered, so the picture is scattering over breadth.
senses.whyCN: 复合词前半意为「宽」，后半意为「散布」，画面就是在宽广范围内撒开。

senses.title: A belief many hold
senses.definition: an opinion accepted by a large share of people
senses.definitionCN: 被很大一部分人接受的看法
senses.example: It is a widespread belief that lightning never strikes the same place twice.
senses.exampleCN: 「闪电不会两次击中同一处」是一种普遍的看法。
senses.why: Beliefs spread through people the way seeds spread through a field, which is why the word fits.
senses.whyCN: 看法在人之间传开，就像种子在田里散开，所以这个词用得贴切。

senses.title: Used by many
senses.definition: in common use across many places or groups
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方或群体中被普遍使用
senses.example: The standard is widespread among manufacturers in three countries.
senses.exampleCN: 这一标准在三个国家的制造商中被广泛采用。
senses.why: Common use is reach translated into hands: the thing is not only present but picked up.
senses.whyCN: 常用是「覆盖」落到了手上：不只存在，而且被拿起来用。

senses.title: Damage across a wide area
senses.definition: destruction covering many places at once
senses.definitionCN: 同时覆盖许多地方的破坏
senses.example: The storm caused widespread damage to roofs and power lines.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴对屋顶和电线造成大范围破坏。
senses.why: Damage takes the word when the area, not the depth, is what strikes observers.
senses.whyCN: 破坏用这个词，是因为触动观察者的是面积，而不是深度。

senses.title: Support from many quarters
senses.definition: backing from many different groups
senses.definitionCN: 来自许多不同群体的支持
senses.example: The proposal drew widespread support from both farmers and city councils.
senses.exampleCN: 该提案得到农民与市议会的广泛支持。
senses.why: Support counts backers, so breadth becomes a political measure.
senses.whyCN: 支持数的是赞成者，广度于是成了政治上的尺度。

senses.title: A disease in many regions
senses.definition: an illness present in many separate regions
senses.definitionCN: 在许多不同地区都存在的疾病
senses.example: The virus became widespread before any vaccine was approved.
senses.exampleCN: 疫苗获批之前，这种病毒已在多地流行。
senses.why: Epidemiology needs a word for reach without severity, and this one supplies it.
senses.whyCN: 流行病学需要一个只讲范围、不讲严重的词，这个词正好补上。

senses.title: A common practice
senses.definition: a custom followed in many places
senses.definitionCN: 在许多地方被沿用的做法
senses.example: Burning fields after harvest is a widespread practice in the valley.
senses.exampleCN: 收割后烧田是这一河谷的普遍做法。
senses.why: A practice spreads by being copied, and reach again decides whether the word fits.
senses.whyCN: 做法靠被模仿而扩散，覆盖范围再次决定这个词是否合适。

senses.title: Shared worry
senses.definition: anxiety felt by many people at once
senses.definitionCN: 许多人同时感到的忧虑
senses.example: There is widespread concern about the falling water table.
senses.exampleCN: 人们对地下水位下降普遍感到担忧。
senses.why: A worry becomes widespread when strangers use the same sentence about it.
senses.whyCN: 当陌生人用同一句话谈论同一件忧心事，它就是普遍的。

intro.en: Widespread is a native English compound of wide and spread, both Old English words, and it has no Latin root. It appeared in written English several centuries ago and has since become the ordinary way to say that something reaches far and reaches many.
intro.cn: 这个词是英语本族复合词，由「宽的」与「散布」两个古英语词构成，没有拉丁词根。它数百年前出现在书面英语里，此后成为表示「传得远、涉及多」的通常说法。

items.en: Wid meant broad in space, and it survives as wide in modern English.
items.cn: 这个词意为空间上的「宽」，在现代英语里仍保存着。

items.en: Spredan meant to spread out, to stretch or scatter.
items.cn: 这个词意为铺开、伸展或撒散。

items.en: The two words were already used together in ordinary speech before they were written as one.
items.cn: 这两个词在写成一体之前，口头上已常一起使用。

items.en: The compound appears in written records for reach across regions; the exact first year is uncertain.
items.cn: 这一复合词在书面记录里出现，用来指跨区域的范围；确切的首次年份不确定。

items.en: News writing made it a staple for trends that cover many places.
items.cn: 新闻写作使它成为描述跨地区趋势的常用词。

items.en: Epidemiology fixed phrases such as widespread transmission, again without a Latin source.
items.cn: 公共卫生领域固定了「广泛传播」等说法，同样没有拉丁来源。

note.en: The first group shares the wide or spread element or looks close; the second group names other kinds of reach. The note also sets widespread against unique, since one word counts places and the other counts copies.
note.cn: 第一组共享「宽」或「散布」成分或形近；第二组指其他「覆盖面」的说法。这里也把「分布广泛的」与「独一无二的」对照：一个数地方，一个数副本。

entries.definition: Broad in space or range.
entries.definitionCN: 指空间或范围上的宽。

entries.definition: Over a large area or among many people.
entries.definitionCN: 指在大范围或许多人中间。

entries.definition: To make or become broader.
entries.definitionCN: 指使变宽或变宽。

entries.definition: To extend over an area, or the extent itself.
entries.definitionCN: 指铺展到一片区域，或指铺展的范围。

entries.definition: Fully open, with nothing blocking the way.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全敞开、无所阻挡。

entries.definition: Existing as the only one of its kind; the opposite way of counting.
entries.definitionCN: 指同类中仅有一个；是另一种计数方式。

entries.definition: Common in a particular place or at a particular time.
entries.definitionCN: 指在某一地方或时期常见。

entries.definition: Spreading through every part of something, often unwelcome.
entries.definitionCN: 指渗透到事物的每一部分，常含不受欢迎之意。

entries.definition: Covering a large area or including much.
entries.definitionCN: 指覆盖面积大或包含内容多。

entries.definition: Widespread and usually unwelcome, as with rumors or disease.
entries.definitionCN: 指广泛存在且通常不受欢迎，如谣言或疾病。

entries.definition: Occurring often, without reference to area.
entries.definitionCN: 指经常发生，不强调地域。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the payment code on every stall, the storm map, the shared worry and the field-burning custom.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用每个摊位上的收款码、风暴影响图、共同的担忧与烧田的习俗。

normal.en: A word that counts places, not copies: how many towns, not how many of each.
normal.cn: 这个词数的是地方，不是份数：数多少个城镇，而不是每处有多少个。

normal.en: A widespread belief is one you hear in three unrelated conversations.
normal.cn: 普遍的看法，是你在三场互不相干的谈话里都听到的说法。

normal.en: A storm map with dots everywhere is a picture of widespread damage.
normal.cn: 风暴图上到处是点，就是大范围破坏的画面。

normal.en: A custom followed in every village is a widespread practice.
normal.cn: 每个村子都沿用的习俗，就是普遍做法。

normal.en: Widespread and unique sit at opposite ends: every place, or only one place.
normal.cn: 「分布广泛」与「独一无二」站在两端：处处都有，或只有一处。

abstract.en: Spread is neutral; the noun after it decides whether the news is good.
abstract.cn: 「散布」本身中性，接在后面的名词决定这消息是好是坏。

abstract.en: Things become widespread faster than the words for judging them.
abstract.cn: 事物变得普遍的速度，快过评判它们的词汇。

abstract.en: A wide thing has many edges, and every edge is somebody's front door.
abstract.cn: 广泛之物有许多边缘，每一处边缘都是某人的家门口。

examples.en: The practice is widespread in the north but rare in the south.
examples.cn: 这种做法在北方普遍，在南方却少见。

examples.en: Widespread use of the drug began only after the trial results were published.
examples.cn: 这种药在试验结果发表后才开始被广泛使用。

examples.en: There was widespread concern that the new rules would favor large firms.
examples.cn: 人们普遍担心新规会偏袒大公司。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「外德斯普瑞德」：一张网「外」面铺得「宽」，撒到哪儿都是，连小摊也不例外

root: 英语本族复合词，由古英语表示「宽」的形容词与表示「散布」的动词构成，没有拉丁词根。十六世纪见于书面记录，确切的首次年份不确定。其反义方向为「独一无二」与「限于一地」。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses count reach rather than number: a wide area, a common belief, common use, broad damage, broad support, a multi-region disease, a common custom, and shared worry.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项数的是覆盖面而不是数量：广大地区、普遍看法、广泛使用、大范围破坏、广泛支持、多地疾病、普遍习俗与共同担忧。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the same payment code on every stall along one county street.
core.cn: 核心意象：县城一条街上每个摊位都贴着同一个收款码。

branches.en: THE SPREAD SURFACE: presence across places, and the customs that travel with it.
branches.cn: 铺开的表面：跨地域的存在，以及随之而行的习俗。

branches.en: THE SHARED MIND: beliefs many hold and worries many feel.
branches.cn: 共享的心思：许多人持有的看法与感受的担忧。

branches.en: THE COMMON TOOL: a standard or product in ordinary use.
branches.cn: 常用的工具：进入日常使用的标准或产品。

branches.en: THE BROAD BLOW: damage that covers many places at once.
branches.cn: 大面积的打击：同时覆盖许多地方的破坏。

branches.en: THE MANY BACKERS AND THE MANY PATIENTS: support, and a disease across regions.
branches.cn: 众多的支持者与众多的病人：支持，以及跨地区的疾病。

intro.en: Widespread is a native compound, so its parts are the ordinary English words wide and spread rather than Latin pieces.
intro.cn: 这个词是本族复合词，构件是普通的英语「宽」与「散布」，而不是拉丁语成分。

latinIntro.en: There is no Latin element in this word; both halves go back to Old English.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有拉丁成分；两半都上溯到古英语。

items.example: It supplies the breadth.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「宽度」。

items.example: The noun made from the same stem.
items.exampleCN: 由同一词干构成的名词。

items.example: The everyday adverb of reach.
items.exampleCN: 表示覆盖范围的常用副词。

items.example: The verb from the same adjective.
items.exampleCN: 由同一形容词构成的动词。

items.example: It supplies the scattering.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「撒开」的意思。

items.example: It marks the second half as a participle.
items.exampleCN: 它把后半标为分词。

items.example: A word built on the second half.
items.exampleCN: 由后半构成的词。

items.example: A rare form, seldom used in writing.
items.exampleCN: 罕见形式，书面少用。

derivatives.zh: 复合词前一成分，义为「宽的」
由「宽的」加副词尾构成，义为「广泛地」
由「宽的」加动词尾构成，义为「加宽」
复合词后一成分，义为「散布」

definition_zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严苛的；严酷的
definition_en: carried out with great care and strict standards, leaving no step unchecked
core_image: 实验室里每份样本都要两个人各自核对，记录上少一行就整批重做
scene: 实验室里，每一批样本都要两人分别核对，任何一步记录不全就得重做。The trial's rigorous protocol required two independent checks for every sample.
sceneCN: 这里指标准严格、不留缺口（第 1 个义项：严格而彻底的）；句意为该试验的严谨规程要求每份样本都做两次独立核对。图中可辨识物件：样本架、双人核对表、签名栏、重做标记。

pos.zh: 严格的；严谨的；严密的；严酷的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「严格地；严谨地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「严格；严谨」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「严格；严酷；严谨」
由同一拉丁动词的另一形容词形式构成，义为「坚硬的；僵化的」
由「僵硬的」加名词尾构成，义为「刚性；僵化」

senses.title: Strict and thorough
senses.definition: done with great care and with no step left unchecked
senses.definitionCN: 以极大的仔细进行，每一步都被核查
senses.example: The safety review was rigorous, and nothing was signed off on trust.
senses.exampleCN: 安全审查十分严格，没有任何一项是靠信任签字的。
senses.why: The Latin root means stiffness, and a stiff procedure does not bend to convenience.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根意为「僵硬」，僵硬的程序不会为图方便而弯折。

senses.title: Demanding testing
senses.definition: testing carried out under hard, controlled conditions
senses.definitionCN: 在严苛且有控制的条件下进行的测试
senses.example: The battery underwent rigorous testing at high and low temperatures.
senses.exampleCN: 电池在高温与低温下接受了严苛测试。
senses.why: Tests are rigorous when the conditions are harder than ordinary use.
senses.whyCN: 当条件比日常使用更苛刻，测试就是严苛的。

senses.title: A proof with no gaps
senses.definition: a proof in which every step is justified
senses.definitionCN: 每一步都有依据的证明
senses.example: A rigorous proof does not rely on a diagram that merely looks right.
senses.exampleCN: 严密的证明不依赖一张只是看起来正确的图。
senses.why: In mathematics the word means the argument cannot be loosened anywhere.
senses.whyCN: 在数学里，这个词意味着论证在任何一处都不能放松。

senses.title: Hard training
senses.definition: training that is physically or mentally severe
senses.definitionCN: 在体力或心力上都很艰苦的训练
senses.example: Rigorous training prepared the crew for a month at sea.
senses.exampleCN: 严酷的训练让船员为海上一个月做好了准备。
senses.why: Training borrows the word because a strict method also trains the will.
senses.whyCN: 训练借用这个词，因为严格的方法也在训练意志。

senses.title: Standards without shortcuts
senses.definition: standards that admit no exceptions for convenience
senses.definitionCN: 不为方便开例外口子的标准
senses.example: The journal applies rigorous standards to every submission, even invited ones.
senses.exampleCN: 该期刊对每篇投稿都适用严格标准，受邀稿也不例外。
senses.why: A standard is rigorous when the exception costs more than the rule.
senses.whyCN: 当例外的代价高于规则，标准才是严格的。

senses.title: Analysis that checks its assumptions
senses.definition: analysis that tests its own assumptions rather than assuming them
senses.definitionCN: 检验自身假设、而不是直接假定成立的分析
senses.example: A rigorous analysis of the survey must first ask who was not asked.
senses.exampleCN: 对这项调查的严谨分析，首先要问谁没有被问到。
senses.why: The analysis turns the strictness on itself, which is the highest form of the method.
senses.whyCN: 分析把严格对准自身，这是该方法最高的形态。

senses.title: Selection by hard tests
senses.definition: choosing only those who pass demanding tests
senses.definitionCN: 只让通过高要求测试者入选
senses.example: The fellowship uses a rigorous selection process with three rounds of review.
senses.exampleCN: 这项奖学金采用三轮评审的严格筛选流程。
senses.why: Selection is rigorous when the gate, not the label, does the choosing.
senses.whyCN: 当做出选择的是门槛而不是标签，筛选才是严格的。

senses.title: Enforcement without leniency
senses.definition: applying a rule fully, with no relaxed exceptions
senses.definitionCN: 完整执行规则，不作宽松的例外
senses.example: Rigorous enforcement of the smoking ban changed behaviour within a month.
senses.exampleCN: 禁烟规定的严格执行在一个月内改变了行为。
senses.why: Enforcement completes the word: the rule now has hands as well as words.
senses.whyCN: 执行补全了这个词：规则如今不光有条文，还有手。

intro.en: Rigorous comes from Latin rigor, stiffness or hardness, from rigere, to be stiff, with an adjective ending that reached English through French. The physical stiffness became a moral and methodological one: a standard that will not bend. The same root also gives rigid and rigor mortis.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 rigor「僵硬、坚硬」，出自 rigere「僵直」，加形容词尾后经法语进入英语。身体上的僵硬变成了道德与方法的僵硬：不肯弯折的标准。同一词根还给出 rigid 与「尸僵」一语。

items.en: Rigere meant to be stiff or numb, said of limbs and of cold.
items.cn: 这个词意为僵直、麻木，用于肢体，也用于寒冷。

items.en: Rigor named stiffness, hardness and, by extension, severity of rule or climate.
items.cn: 这个词指僵硬、坚硬，并引申指规则或气候的严酷。

items.en: Later Latin formed an adjective meaning full of stiffness or severity.
items.cn: 后起拉丁语构成形容词，意为「充满僵硬或严酷的」。

items.en: French carried the adjective into the language of law and method.
items.cn: 法语把该形容词带入法律与方法的语言。

items.en: English applied it to rules, proofs and training.
items.cn: 英语把它用于规则、证明与训练。

items.en: Research methods fixed phrases such as rigorous testing; the first date of each is uncertain.
items.cn: 科研方法固定了「严苛测试」等说法；各自首见的年代不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the stiffness root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of strictness. The note warns that vigorous looks like a relative but comes from a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「僵硬」词根或形近；第二组指其他「严格」的说法。这里提醒：形近的「精力充沛」一词出自另一词根，并非同族。

entries.definition: Strictness or severity, and in medicine, a chill.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格或严酷，医学上指寒战。

entries.definition: Stiff and unable to bend, literally or in attitude.
entries.definitionCN: 指僵硬不能弯，字面或态度上皆可。

entries.definition: In a strict and thorough way.
entries.definitionCN: 指以严格而彻底的方式。

entries.definition: The quality of being strict and thorough.
entries.definitionCN: 指严格而彻底的性质。

entries.definition: Full of energy and strength; its root means to be lively, not stiff.
entries.definitionCN: 指精力充沛、强健；其词根意为「有生气」，并非「僵硬」。

entries.definition: Insisting on exact obedience to rules.
entries.definitionCN: 指坚持对规则的精确遵守。

entries.definition: Complete, with no part left out.
entries.definitionCN: 指完整、没有遗漏任何部分。

entries.definition: Showing extreme attention to small details.
entries.definitionCN: 指对细小处极度注意。

entries.definition: Tight and demanding, often of rules or conditions.
entries.definitionCN: 指紧而苛刻，多用于规则或条件。

entries.definition: Demanding a great deal of effort or precision.
entries.definitionCN: 指要求大量努力或精确。

entries.definition: Harsh in force or treatment.
entries.definitionCN: 指在力度或对待上严厉。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the two signature lines, the frozen joint, the long proof and the three-round review.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用两行签名、冻僵的关节、冗长的证明与三轮评审。

normal.en: A rigorous process has two signatures where one would do.
normal.cn: 严谨的流程在一个签名够用的地方放两个。

normal.en: Rigid means the joint will not bend; rigorous means the rule will not bend.
normal.cn: 「僵硬的」说关节不弯，「严格的」说规则不弯。

normal.en: A rigorous proof leaves no step to the reader's goodwill.
normal.cn: 严密的证明不把任何一步留给读者的善意。

normal.en: Rigorous training is remembered in the body, not in the notes.
normal.cn: 严酷的训练被记在身体里，而不是记在笔记里。

normal.en: Vigorous is about energy and rigorous is about stiffness, though they sound alike.
normal.cn: 「强健的」讲精力，「严格的」讲僵硬，尽管读音相似。

abstract.en: Strictness is a promise that the result will not depend on who was watching.
abstract.cn: 严格是一种承诺：结果不取决于当时谁在看。

abstract.en: The same stiffness that protects a result can freeze a field for a generation.
abstract.cn: 保护结果的那种僵硬，也可能把一个领域冻住一代人。

abstract.en: A rigorous standard is expensive, which is why it is often replaced by its description.
abstract.cn: 严格的标准很贵，所以常被它的描述所取代。

examples.en: The claim survived rigorous testing by three independent laboratories.
examples.cn: 这一主张经受了三家独立实验室的严苛测试。

examples.en: Her analysis was rigorous, and it questioned the survey's own assumptions.
examples.cn: 她的分析很严谨，也质疑了调查自身的假设。

examples.en: Rigorous enforcement, not new rules, reduced the accident rate.
examples.cn: 降低事故率的是严格执行，而不是新规则。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「瑞格若斯」：规矩「硬」得像冻住的关节，一步也不肯弯，检查才做得严

root: 源于拉丁语表示「僵直」的动词，其名词义为「僵硬、严酷」，后起形容词再经法语进入英语。同族有表示「严格」「僵硬的」「刚性」的词；形近而表示「精力充沛」的词出自表示「有生气」的另一词根。十六世纪进入英语；各技术短语首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses turn stiffness into method: a thorough procedure, demanding tests, gapless proofs, hard training, standards without shortcuts, self-checking analysis, strict selection, and full enforcement.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项把「僵硬」变成方法：彻底的流程、严苛的测试、无缺口的证明、艰苦的训练、不许走捷径的标准、自查假设的分析、严格筛选与完整执行。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two signatures on every sheet, and a whole batch is redone if one line is missing.
core.cn: 核心意象：每张记录上两个签名，少一行就整批重做。

branches.en: THE STIFF PROCEDURE: care that refuses convenience in every ordinary step.
branches.cn: 僵硬的程序：在每个寻常步骤上都不为方便让步。

branches.en: THE HARD TEST AND THE HARD DRILL: strict conditions, and training built under them.
branches.cn: 严苛的测试与艰苦的训练：严格的条件，以及在条件下筑起的训练。

branches.en: THE CLOSED ARGUMENT: proofs and analyses with no step left to goodwill.
branches.cn: 封闭的论证：不把任何一步留给善意的证明与分析。

branches.en: THE UNBENDING RULE: standards and enforcement that admit no exceptions.
branches.cn: 不肯弯的规则：不容例外开的标准与执行。

branches.en: THE NARROW GATE: selection that only lets the tested through.
branches.cn: 窄门：只让过关者进入的筛选。

intro.en: Rigorous is a Latin stiffness noun with an adjective ending; its family covers rigidity, strictness and the adverb.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「僵硬」名词加形容词尾；词族覆盖刚性、严格与副词。

latinIntro.en: Latin rigere and rigor supply the stiffness, and the later adjective rigorosus gives the English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「僵直」与「僵硬」提供词干，后起形容词给出英语形态。

items.example: The oldest root of the family.
items.exampleCN: 这是词族最古老的根。

items.example: It gives English rigor.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语的「严格」。

items.example: It gives the English adjective its shape.
items.exampleCN: 它给出英语形容词的形态。

items.example: It marks the word as an adjective.
items.exampleCN: 它把该词标为形容词。

items.example: It forms rigorously.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「严格地」。

items.example: It forms rigorousness.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「严谨」。

items.example: A same-root word from a different form.
items.exampleCN: 同词根但由另一形式构成的词。

items.example: Built on rigid, not on rigorous.
items.exampleCN: 由「僵硬的」构成，而非由本词构成。

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「严格地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「严谨」
由同一拉丁词干构成，义为「严格；严酷」
由同一拉丁动词的另一形容词形式构成，义为「僵硬的」

definition_zh: 过时的；不再使用的；被淘汰的；废弃的；（词、法规）已不通用的
definition_en: no longer used or accepted because something newer has replaced it
core_image: 仓库角落一箱旧式接口零件还在，新到的设备上已经找不到能插进去的孔
scene: 仓库角落里还堆着一箱旧式接口零件，新到的设备上已经找不到能插进去的孔。The warehouse still holds obsolete connectors that no current device accepts.
sceneCN: 这里指已被淘汰、不再使用（第 1 个义项：不再使用的）；句意为仓库里仍存着没有一台现役设备能接上的过时接口件。图中可辨识物件：仓库角落、旧接口零件箱、新设备、无法插入的端口。

pos.zh: 过时的；不再使用的；废弃的；被淘汰的
（少用）使废弃；使过时

derivatives.zh: 由该词干加表示过程的名词尾构成，义为「废弃；淘汰过程」
由该词干加表示「正在……的」词尾构成，义为「正逐渐淘汰的」
由该词干加动词尾构成，义为「逐渐废弃；变得过时」
由「计划的」与该名词构成，义为「有计划地使产品过时」

senses.title: No longer used
senses.definition: no longer used because something newer has taken its place
senses.definitionCN: 由于有更新之物取代而不再使用
senses.example: Gas lamps became obsolete when electric light reached the streets.
senses.exampleCN: 电灯进入街道后，煤气灯就不再使用了。
senses.why: The Latin participle means grown out of use, and this sense is its plainest survival.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁分词意为「变得不被使用」，这一义项是最直白的延续。

senses.title: A word fallen out of use
senses.definition: a word that people no longer say except when reading old texts
senses.definitionCN: 人们除读旧文外已不再说的词
senses.example: The dictionary marks the word as obsolete after 1700.
senses.exampleCN: 词典把这个词标为 1700 年后已废弃。
senses.why: Language change produces the same effect as machinery: the old form still exists, but nobody reaches for it.
senses.whyCN: 语言变化造成的效果和机器一样：旧形式还在，只是没人再去取用。

senses.title: A rule no longer in force
senses.definition: a regulation that has been replaced or withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 已被替换或撤销的规章
senses.example: The clause is obsolete and should be struck from the contract.
senses.exampleCN: 该条款已失效，应从合同中删去。
senses.why: Law keeps obsolete clauses on paper long after practice has left them.
senses.whyCN: 实践早已离开的条款，法律仍让它们留在纸上。

senses.title: A superseded machine
senses.definition: equipment that newer models have made impractical to keep
senses.definitionCN: 新机型使其继续保留已不实用的设备
senses.example: Spare parts for the obsolete printer now cost more than a new one.
senses.exampleCN: 那台淘汰打印机的配件，现在比买新的还贵。
senses.why: A machine is obsolete when fixing it costs more than replacing it.
senses.whyCN: 当修理比替换更贵，机器就被淘汰了。

senses.title: An idea left behind
senses.definition: a belief that no longer fits current knowledge
senses.definitionCN: 不再符合当今知识的看法
senses.example: The idea that memory is a single store is obsolete.
senses.exampleCN: 认为记忆是单一仓库的看法已经过时。
senses.why: Ideas age without breaking, which is why the word fits them so well.
senses.whyCN: 观念不会坏，只会老，所以这个词用在他们身上特别贴切。

senses.title: Old stock still on the shelf
senses.definition: goods kept in storage although nobody now buys them
senses.definitionCN: 虽仍存放、如今却无人购买的货物
senses.example: The shop wrote off its obsolete stock at the end of the year.
senses.exampleCN: 商店在年末把积压的淘汰存货核销。
senses.why: Stock becomes obsolete while it is still perfectly new in the box.
senses.whyCN: 存货在盒子里还崭新时，就已经成了淘汰货。

senses.title: A retired unit or currency
senses.definition: a unit of money or measure that has been withdrawn
senses.definitionCN: 已被停用的货币或计量单位
senses.example: Prices were still quoted in an obsolete currency after the reform.
senses.exampleCN: 改革之后，标价仍用已经停用的货币。
senses.why: Money and measures can be withdrawn by decree, and then the word is official.
senses.whyCN: 货币与单位可由法令停用，这时这个词是官方用语。

senses.title: A practice abandoned
senses.definition: a way of doing things that has been given up
senses.definitionCN: 已经被放弃的做事方式
senses.example: Hand-copying records by ink became obsolete once the database went live.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库上线后，用墨水手抄记录的做法就被废弃了。
senses.why: A habit disappears when the tool that carried it disappears first.
senses.whyCN: 当承载习惯的工具先消失，习惯也随之消失。

intro.en: Obsolete comes from Latin obsoletus, grown old or worn out, the past participle of obsolescere, to fall into disuse. The verb is usually explained as ob-, away, plus solere, to be accustomed, though the exact force of the prefix is described differently by different sources. English took the adjective in the sixteenth century.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 obsoletus「变旧、用坏」，是动词 obsolescere「渐不用」的过去分词。该动词通常解释为「离开」加「习惯于」，但前缀的具体作用各家说法不一。英语在十六世纪吸收了该形容词。

items.en: Solere meant to be accustomed or to be in the habit, and it stands behind the idea of usual practice.
items.cn: 这个词意为「习惯于、常有此习」，是「惯常做法」这一观念背后的词。

items.en: The verb meant to wear out or fall out of use, and its prefix suggests moving away from what was usual.
items.cn: 该动词意为用坏或渐不用，其前缀暗示从惯常状态离开。

items.en: The participle described what had already grown old and was no longer wanted.
items.cn: 该分词形容已经变旧、不再被需要之物。

items.en: French used the adjective for words and customs that had dropped away.
items.cn: 法语用它指已经消失的词与习俗。

items.en: English extended it from words to machines, laws and ideas.
items.cn: 英语把它从词语扩展到机器、法规与观念。

items.en: Manufacturing gave it the compound planned obsolescence; the phrase's first year is uncertain.
items.cn: 制造业给出复合说法「有计划地淘汰」；该说法首见的年份不确定。

note.en: The first group shares the grown-out-of-use root or looks close; the second group names other kinds of being out of date. The note warns that absolute is a look-alike from an unrelated root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「用旧而废」词根或形近；第二组指其他「过时」的说法。这里提醒：形近的「绝对」一词出自不相干的词根。

entries.definition: The process of becoming outdated.
entries.definitionCN: 指逐渐过时的过程。

entries.definition: In the process of becoming obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 指正在走向淘汰的。

entries.definition: To grow obsolete.
entries.definitionCN: 指变得过时。

entries.definition: Complete and unconditional; it comes from a verb meaning to loosen or set free, not from being accustomed.
entries.definitionCN: 指完全且无条件的；出自表示「解开、释放」的动词，与「习惯于」无关。

entries.definition: Old-fashioned but possibly still usable.
entries.definitionCN: 指样式老但可能仍可使用。

entries.definition: Very old and no longer suitable, often said of systems.
entries.definitionCN: 指非常老旧且已不适用，常用于制度。

entries.definition: No longer in fashion or no longer the accepted way.
entries.definitionCN: 指不再流行或不再是被接受的方式。

entries.definition: No longer existing or operating, said of organizations.
entries.definitionCN: 指已不存在或停止运作，用于机构。

entries.definition: Replaced by something that does the job better.
entries.definitionCN: 指被做得更好的东西取代。

entries.definition: Belonging to an earlier period and retained only in special contexts.
entries.definitionCN: 指属于较早时期、只在特殊语境中保留。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the box of connectors, the gas lamp, the struck-out contract clause and the written-off stock.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用那箱接口件、煤气灯、被划掉的合同条款与核销的存货。

normal.en: Obsolete does not mean broken; it means nobody reaches for it any more.
normal.cn: 「过时」不等于坏了，而是没人再去取用它。

normal.en: A gas lamp still lights, but the street is wired for electricity.
normal.cn: 煤气灯仍能亮，可街上已经通了电。

normal.en: The word and the machine share one fate: both are outgrown.
normal.cn: 词语与机器命运相同：都被长过了头。

normal.en: Planned obsolescence is obsolescence with a schedule and a budget.
normal.cn: 「有计划地淘汰」，就是带着日程与预算的淘汰。

normal.en: Absolute looks close but belongs to loosening, not to growing old.
normal.cn: 形近的那个词属于「解开」，不属于「变旧」。

abstract.en: Usefulness is a relationship between a thing and a moment, and moments move.
abstract.cn: 有用是物与时刻之间的关系，而时刻会走。

abstract.en: Every generation inherits tools it must first learn to stop using.
abstract.cn: 每一代人都继承了一批必须先学会不再使用的工具。

abstract.en: What becomes obsolete usually leaves a word behind that outlives it.
abstract.cn: 被淘汰的东西，往往留下一个比它活得更久的词。

examples.en: The format is obsolete, and the archive can no longer open the files.
examples.cn: 这种格式已经过时，档案馆再也打不开那些文件。

examples.en: New scanning software rendered the old index cards obsolete overnight.
examples.cn: 新的扫描软件一夜之间让旧索引卡被淘汰。

examples.en: Using that term today sounds obsolete even in legal writing.
examples.cn: 今天再用那个词，即便在法律文书里也显得过时。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「奥伯索利特」：旧东西还在架上，只是没人再伸手去拿，慢慢就「废」了

root: 源于拉丁语表示「习惯于」的动词，其复合动词义为「渐不用、用坏」，过去分词义为「变旧废弃的」，经法语进入英语。该前缀的具体作用各家解释不一。十六世纪进入英语；「有计划地淘汰」一语首见年份不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow disuse: an unused thing, a dead word, a withdrawn rule, a superseded machine, a left-behind idea, unsold stock, a retired unit, and an abandoned practice.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「不再使用」展开：闲置之物、废弃的词、撤销的规定、被取代的机器、被抛下的观念、卖不掉的存货、停用的单位与放弃的做法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the box of connectors that no new machine has a port for.
core.cn: 核心意象：一箱接口件，新机器上找不到能插的孔。

branches.en: THE RETIRED THING: an object or machine that newer things replaced.
branches.cn: 退役之物：被更新之物取代的器物或机器。

branches.en: THE RETIRED WORD AND IDEA: what people no longer say or believe.
branches.cn: 退役的词与观念：人们不再说、也不再信的东西。

branches.en: THE CLAUSE LEFT ON PAPER: a rule that practice has already abandoned.
branches.cn: 留在纸上的条款：实践早已放弃的规则。

branches.en: THE SHELF AND THE HABIT: stock nobody buys, practices nobody follows.
branches.cn: 货架与习惯：无人购买的存货、无人沿用的做法。

branches.en: THE WITHDRAWN UNIT: money or measures taken out of use by decree.
branches.cn: 撤销的单位：由法令停用的货币或计量单位。

intro.en: Obsolete is a Latin participle used as an English adjective; its family covers the process of going out of use and the schedule that produces it.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁分词用作英语形容词；词族覆盖「走向废弃」的过程，以及制造这一过程的日程。

latinIntro.en: Latin solere and obsolescere supply the habit and the falling away from it; the participle obsoletus gives the English form.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「习惯于」与「渐不用」提供「习惯」与「离开习惯」两层意思；分词给出英语形态。

items.example: It supplies the idea of usual practice.
items.exampleCN: 它提供「惯常做法」的意思。

items.example: It marks movement away from the usual.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「离开常态」的方向。

items.example: The verb of decay behind the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是词背后的「衰废」动词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective directly.
items.exampleCN: 它直接给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It forms obsolescence.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「淘汰过程」。

items.example: It forms obsolescent.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「正走向淘汰的」。

items.example: It forms the rare verb obsolesce.
items.exampleCN: 它构成少用的动词「变得过时」。

items.example: A commercial phrase built on the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 由该形容词构成的商业说法。

derivatives.zh: 由该词干加表示过程的名词尾构成，义为「淘汰过程」
由该词干加表示「正在……」的词尾构成，义为「正走向淘汰的」
由该词干加动词尾构成，义为「变得过时」
由「计划的」与该名词构成，义为「有计划地使产品过时」

definition_zh: 错综复杂的；繁复精细的；盘根错节的；精巧的
definition_en: having many small parts or connections arranged in a way that is hard to follow
core_image: 老式钟表被打开的瞬间，一层层齿轮彼此咬合，每一枚都牵动另一枚
scene: 老式钟表被打开，里面一层层齿轮彼此咬合，每一枚都牵动另一枚。Restorers spent weeks on the intricate gearing inside the old clock.
sceneCN: 这里指部件繁多、彼此交错（第 1 个义项：部件彼此咬合的）；句意为修复师花了数周处理这只旧钟表繁复精细的齿轮结构。图中可辨识物件：打开的钟表、层层齿轮、咬合齿纹、放大镜。

pos.zh: 错综复杂的；繁复精细的；盘根错节的

derivatives.zh: 由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「错综；繁复」
由该形容词加副词尾构成，义为「错综复杂地；精细地」
由该形容词加表示性质的名词尾构成，义为「错综」，较少用
由表示「向外」的前缀加同一拉丁词干构成，义为「解脱；拔出」，是同一词根的相反方向

senses.title: Many interlocking parts
senses.definition: having many parts that depend on one another
senses.definitionCN: 拥有许多相互依赖的部件
senses.example: The engine's intricate parts had to be numbered before it was opened.
senses.exampleCN: 发动机拆开之前，那些彼此咬合的零件都得编号。
senses.why: The Latin verb meant to entangle, and this sense keeps the picture of threads crossed over one another.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词意为「缠结」，这一义项保留的就是线彼此交叉的画面。

senses.title: A detailed pattern
senses.definition: a design with many fine lines woven together
senses.definitionCN: 由许多细线交织而成的图样
senses.example: The shawl is famous for its intricate border of vines and birds.
senses.exampleCN: 这条披肩以藤鸟交织的繁复花边闻名。
senses.why: The pattern is intricate because the eye must travel along every line.
senses.whyCN: 图案错综，因为眼睛必须沿着每一条线走。

senses.title: Fine details
senses.definition: small features that must be followed one by one
senses.definitionCN: 必须逐一追究的细小特征
senses.example: The agreement is full of intricate details about who pays for what.
senses.exampleCN: 协议里满是关于谁付哪笔钱的繁复细节。
senses.why: Details are intricate when they cannot be understood one at a time.
senses.whyCN: 细节错综，是因为它们无法一件一件地单独理解。

senses.title: A tangled plot
senses.definition: a story whose threads cross and return
senses.definitionCN: 线索彼此交叉又回返的故事
senses.example: The novel's intricate plot keeps three families in view at once.
senses.exampleCN: 这部小说情节错综，同时盯着三个家庭。
senses.why: A plot is intricate when its threads return to the same scene from different sides.
senses.whyCN: 情节错综，是当它的线索从不同方向回到同一场景。

senses.title: Complex machinery
senses.definition: a machine with many small linked mechanisms
senses.definitionCN: 由许多相互连接的小机构组成的机器
senses.example: The loom's intricate mechanism was rebuilt from a single photograph.
senses.exampleCN: 这台织机的复杂机构是凭一张照片重建的。
senses.why: Machinery earns the word when every part seems to be holding another.
senses.whyCN: 当每个部件似乎都在托住另一个，机器就用得上这个词。

senses.title: A complicated problem
senses.definition: a problem with many causes that cannot be separated easily
senses.definitionCN: 原因众多且难以分开的问题
senses.example: Land rights in the valley are intricate, with claims overlapping for centuries.
senses.exampleCN: 这一河谷的土地权属盘根错节，各方主张重叠了数百年。
senses.why: Problems are intricate when the causes cannot be pulled apart without breaking them.
senses.whyCN: 当原因一拆就断，问题就是盘根错节的。

senses.title: An involved relationship
senses.definition: a relationship with many overlapping obligations
senses.definitionCN: 义务彼此重叠的关系
senses.example: The two firms share an intricate web of suppliers and loans.
senses.exampleCN: 两家公司共享一张由供应商与贷款组成的错综网络。
senses.why: Relationships become intricate through obligations that overlap rather than multiply.
senses.whyCN: 关系因义务重叠、而不是数量增多，才变得错综。

senses.title: Fine workmanship
senses.definition: made with delicate, careful work on a small scale
senses.definitionCN: 在小尺度上以细致功夫完成的
senses.example: The intricate carving on the door took a craftsman a whole winter.
senses.exampleCN: 门上精细的雕刻花了工匠一整个冬天。
senses.why: Workmanship is intricate when smallness and care appear together.
senses.whyCN: 当细小与用心同时出现，工艺就是精细的。

intro.en: Intricate comes from Latin intricatus, the past participle of intricare, to entangle, built on in- and tricae, trifles or perplexities. The word entered English through the idea of a knot rather than through that of size, so intricacy is about threads crossing, not merely about many pieces.
intro.cn: 这个词来自拉丁语 intricatus，是动词 intricare「缠结」的过去分词，由「进入」与 tricae「琐碎、纠葛」构成。它经「打结」的观念而非「数量多」的观念进入英语，所以「错综」讲的是线交叉，而不只是零件多。

items.en: Tricae meant trifles, tricks or perplexities, the stuff that catches a person up.
items.cn: 这个词意为琐事、诡计或纠葛，也就是把人缠住的东西。

items.en: The verb meant to entangle or involve, literally to put someone into the tricae.
items.cn: 该动词意为缠住、卷入，字面就是把人放进纠葛之中。

items.en: The participle described something entangled, and it passed into English as an adjective.
items.cn: 该分词形容被缠住之物，作为形容词进入英语。

items.en: English used it for plots, designs and arguments that are hard to follow.
items.cn: 英语用它指难以追循的情节、图样与论证。

items.en: Craft writing applied it to carving and metalwork of many fine parts.
items.cn: 工艺写作把它用于多细部的雕刻与金工。

items.en: Systems and law gave it new subjects; the relation of English trick to the same Latin word is debated rather than settled.
items.cn: 制度与法律给出新的对象；英语中表示「诡计」的形近词是否同出这一拉丁词，各家有争论而无定论。

note.en: The first group shares the tangle root or looks close; the second names other kinds of complexity. The note also separates intricate from complicated and warns about intrinsic, which looks close but has a different root.
note.cn: 第一组共享「缠结」词根或形近；第二组指其他「复杂」的说法。这里也把「错综」与「复杂」辨析，并提醒形近的「内在的」一词出自另一词根。

entries.definition: The quality of being entangled or finely detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 指错综或精细的性质。

entries.definition: In a way that is finely woven or detailed.
entries.definitionCN: 指以精细交织的方式。

entries.definition: To free from a tangle; the prefix means out of.
entries.definitionCN: 指从缠结中解脱；前缀意为「向外」。

entries.definition: To fascinate or to plot secretly; from the same tangle word through French or Italian, though the route is debated.
entries.definitionCN: 指使人着迷或暗中谋划；经法语或意大利语同出这一「缠结」词，具体路径有争论。

entries.definition: Belonging to a thing by its own nature; its root means inward, not entangled.
entries.definitionCN: 指按本性属于某物；其词根意为「向内」，与「缠结」无关。

entries.definition: Made hard to understand by many parts folded together; it stresses difficulty rather than fine work.
entries.definitionCN: 指因许多部分折在一起而难懂；强调的是难，而非精细。

entries.definition: Having parts that are closely connected, often as a neutral description.
entries.definitionCN: 指各部分紧密相连，常为中性描述。

entries.definition: Worked out with many carefully arranged details.
entries.definitionCN: 指经过精心安排、细节繁多。

entries.definition: Showing many small facts, without implying that they interlock.
entries.definitionCN: 指呈现许多细小事实，不暗示彼此咬合。

entries.definition: Twisted and hard to follow, often with disapproval.
entries.definitionCN: 指曲折难循，常含贬义。

entries.definition: Having many parts or connections, sometimes hard to explain.
entries.definitionCN: 指部分或关联很多，有时难以说明。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations use the opened clock, the vine border, the tangled land claims and the winter of carving.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想使用打开的钟表、藤蔓花边、缠结的土地主张与雕了一冬的门。

normal.en: Intricate things are not just many; they are tied to one another.
normal.cn: 错综之物不只是多，而是彼此拴在一起。

normal.en: Turn one gear and the next answers, which is what makes the whole thing intricate.
normal.cn: 转动一枚齿轮，下一枚就应声而动，这才让整体错综。

normal.en: A shawl's border is intricate because the vines hold the birds.
normal.cn: 披肩花边错综，是因为藤蔓把鸟扣在了一起。

normal.en: Intricate details are the ones you must follow in order, not just count.
normal.cn: 繁复的细节要按顺序追究，而不只是数一数。

normal.en: Intricate praises the weaving; complicated complains about the difficulty.
normal.cn: 「错综」在称许织法，「复杂」在抱怨难度。

abstract.en: A tangle is order that has not yet been read.
abstract.cn: 缠结是尚未被读懂的秩序。

abstract.en: The same root gives extricate, because every knot also implies a way out.
abstract.cn: 同一词根给出「解脱」，因为每个结都暗示着一条出路。

abstract.en: What is intricate rewards patience and punishes haste, which is why it survives in craft.
abstract.cn: 错综之物奖赏耐心、惩罚急躁，所以它在工艺里留了下来。

examples.en: The carpet's intricate pattern was copied from a sixteenth-century drawing.
examples.cn: 这块地毯的繁复图案摹自一幅十六世纪的图样。

examples.en: The case involves an intricate set of overlapping contracts.
examples.cn: 该案涉及一组盘根错节、彼此重叠的合同。

examples.en: Restorers spent weeks on the intricate gearing inside the old clock.
examples.cn: 修复师花了数周处理这只旧钟表繁复精细的齿轮结构。

dict_mnemonic.text: 读作「因吹卡特」：线一「缠」就成结，结里又有结，越看越细，越细越难拆

root: 源于拉丁语表示「琐事、纠葛」的名词，其动词义为「缠住、使卷入」，过去分词进入英语作形容词。同族有表示「错综」的名词与表示「解脱」的动词；形近而表示「内在的」的词出自表示「向内」的另一词根。英语中表示「诡计」的词是否同出这一拉丁词，各家有争论而无定论。十五世纪进入英语；各技术用法首见年代不确定。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses follow the tangle: interlocking parts, a woven pattern, fine details, a tangled plot, complex machinery, a problem with many causes, an overlapped relationship, and delicate workmanship.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项沿着「缠结」展开：彼此咬合的部件、交织的图案、繁复细节、错综情节、复杂机械、多因问题、重叠的关系与精细工艺。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the clock opens and every gear is held by the teeth of the next one.
core.cn: 核心意象：钟表打开，每一枚齿轮都被下一枚的齿咬住。

branches.en: THE INTERLOCKED MACHINE: parts that hold one another, from clocks to looms.
branches.cn: 咬合的机器：彼此扣住的部件，从钟表到织机。

branches.en: THE FINE HAND: woven patterns and carving that reward close looking.
branches.cn: 精细的手：值得细看的织纹与雕刻。

branches.en: THE DETAILS IN ORDER: small features that must be followed one by one.
branches.cn: 按序的细节：必须逐一追究的细小特征。

branches.en: THE RETURNING PLOT: threads that cross and come back to the same scene.
branches.cn: 回返的情节：交叉之后又回到同一场景的线索。

branches.en: THE KNOTTED WORLD: problems and relationships whose causes overlap.
branches.cn: 打结的世界：原因彼此重叠的问题与关系。

intro.en: Intricate is a Latin tangle verb with a participle ending; its family covers the noun of tangling and the verb of getting free.
intro.cn: 这个词是拉丁语「缠结」动词加分词词尾；词族覆盖「缠结」的名词与「解脱」的动词。

latinIntro.en: Latin tricae and intricare supply the knot, and the participle intricatus gives the English adjective.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语的「纠葛」与「缠住」提供那个结，分词给出英语形容词。

items.example: The knot at the centre of the word.
items.exampleCN: 这是词中央的那个结。

items.example: It marks putting someone into the tangle.
items.exampleCN: 它标出「把人放进缠结」。

items.example: The verb behind the adjective.
items.exampleCN: 这是形容词背后的动词。

items.example: It gives the English adjective directly.
items.exampleCN: 它直接给出这个英语形容词。

items.example: It marks the participle shape.
items.exampleCN: 它标出分词的形态。

items.example: It forms intricacy.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「错综」。

items.example: It forms intricately.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「错综地」。

items.example: It forms extricate, the way out of the tangle.
items.exampleCN: 它构成「解脱」，即从缠结里出来的路。
